column5: He clutches the pendent close to his chest.
column6: 他把吊坠紧紧贴在胸前。

column5: Would you sit with me, [firstname]?\nWe might be here for a while, after all.
column6: 你愿意陪我坐一会儿吗，[firstname]？\n毕竟，我们可能要在这里待上一阵子。

column5: He sits down on the ground, attracting stares from a few passers-by.{w}\nI join him, caring more for his well-being than the judgment of those around us.{w}\nLooking down at the ground, he places the pendent down, and moves it around slightly.
column6: 他在地上坐下，引来几个路人的注视。{w}\n我在他身旁坐下，比起旁人的眼光，我更在意他的身心。{w}\n他低头看着地面，把吊坠放下，又轻轻拨弄了几下。

column5: It was... right here, I think.\nYou never really forget, you know?\nI hope it's not weird to sit here with me.
column6: 就是……这里吧，我想。\n有些事你永远不会真的忘记，你知道吗？\n希望陪我坐在这儿不会让你觉得奇怪。

column5: I shake my head, and let him do what he needs to do.
column6: 我摇了摇头，让他去做他需要做的事。

column5: Coming here, to face what happened — I needed to do this.\nBut now I'm not sure what to do next. I mean, with the pendent.\nDo I leave it behind...? Just like my memories? Or do I hold on?
column6: 回到这里，去面对发生过的事——这是我必须做的。\n但事到如今，我不确定接下来该怎么做。我是说，这枚吊坠。\n我该把它留下吗……？就像我的记忆一样？还是该继续留着？

column5: That was a good question, and I can tell it's bothering him.
column6: 这是个好问题，我看得出它正困扰着他。

column5: I'm sure someone will just come around and steal it, anyway.\nBut maybe that's for the best. It can be somebody else's burden.\nI think I've grown tired of carrying it around for my entire life.
column6: 反正总会有人路过把它偷走的。\n但也许那样最好。让它成为别人的负担吧。\n我想，我已经厌倦了一辈子都带着它。

column5: However, I also don't want to regret doing this.\nI could be acting rashly in the face of our final battle.\nIt wouldn't be the first time somebody has done that, you know?
column6: 可是，我也不想为这件事后悔。\n面对最后的决战，我可能是在冲动行事。\n这种傻事，别人也不是第一次干了，你懂吗？

column5: I nod, and let him speak.
column6: 我点点头，让他继续说下去。

column5: Look at me. The world is at stake, and I'm worried about {i}this{/i}.\nYou know what? With everything you've done for us — I trust you.\nWhat do you think I should do, [firstname]? Take it, or leave it...?
column6: 看看我。世界都危在旦夕了，我却在为{i}这个{/i}发愁。\n你知道吗？看在你为我们做的一切份上——我信你。\n你觉得我该怎么做，[firstname]？带走，还是留下……？

column5: Besides, I'm a bit biased here in almost every regard.\nYour head is more clear than mine, so it's worth a shot.\nWhat do you think I should do here? What's the right choice?
column6: 再说，这件事我几乎在各方面都夹带着私心。\n你比我头脑清醒，所以值得一试。\n你觉得我该怎么做？什么才是正确的选择？

column5: You're probably right; and I don't want to make a mistake.\nPerhaps just coming here after all those years was enough.\nYou have no idea how much this means to me, [firstname].
column6: 你说得大概没错；我不想犯错。\n也许隔了这么多年，光是回到这里就已经足够了。\n你根本不知道这对我来说意味着什么，[firstname]。

column5: He picks the pendent up off the ground, and clutches it in his hand.{w}\nWe both stand up, and turn back in the direction we came from.
column6: 他把吊坠从地上拾起，攥在手心。{w}\n我们双双站起，转身朝来时的方向走去。

column5: You're right. I think this is something I need to do.\nIt'll be hard, but I need to move on. I can't hold myself back.\nWe're fighting to liberate our world, and push forward, right?
column6: 你说得对。我想这件事我必须去做。\n会很难，但我得向前看。我不能拖住自己。\n我们是在为解放这个世界而战，要一路向前，对吧？

column5: It's a bit hypocritical for me to do the opposite to myself.\nI hope whoever picks it up goes on to take good care of it.\nIt means a lot to me, and I hope it can do that for others, too.
column6: 要是我对自己做相反的事，那就有点虚伪了。\n希望捡到它的人能好好珍惜。\n它对我来说意义重大，也希望它能为别人带来同样的意义。

column5: He places his hand on the pendent, touching it one last time.
column6: 他把手覆在吊坠上，最后一次触碰它。

column5: It's time for me to let go, Mother.\nThis was always yours. I was just... holding on to it for a while.\nI'll miss you, always. But your sacrifice for me will {i}never{/i} be forgotten.
column6: 是时候放手了，母亲。\n它一直都是你的。我只是……替你保管了一阵子。\n我会永远想念你。但你为我所做的牺牲，{i}永远{/i}不会被遗忘。

column5: He smiles, and lets go of the pendent. It shimmers in the sun.{w}\nWe both stand up, and turn back in the direction we came from.
column6: 他笑了笑，松开了吊坠。它在阳光下微微闪光。{w}\n我们双双站起，转身朝来时的方向走去。

column5: Well then, should we get going?
column6: 那么，我们该走了吗？

column5: I nod, and we start walking back the way we came.{w}\nBut Damek looks much happier and content than he did earlier.{w}\nPerhaps the events of today would give him a clear mind in the future.
column6: 我点点头，我们沿着来路往回走。{w}\n但达梅克看起来比刚才开心、满足了许多。{w}\n也许今天的事，会让他在将来保持清醒的头脑。

column5: As our final battle was imminent — we would find out sooner rather than later.
column6: 最后的决战近在眼前——答案很快就会揭晓。

column5: Howl enters my quarters, carrying an aura of purpose with him.{w}\nAfter Eastcrown, I know that something big has been on his mind.{w}\nWe were so close to the final battle. It was probably time for us to talk.
column6: 豪尔走进我的房间，带着一股心意已决的气场。{w}\n经历了东冠之后，我知道他心里一直压着一件大事。{w}\n决战已近在咫尺。也许我们该谈谈了。

column5: Monarch? We must speak with you.\nIt's about our upcoming attack on Balteus.\nAt least, we think it is. Things have been complicated.
column6: 君主？我们必须和你谈谈。\n是关于即将对巴尔泰乌斯发动的进攻。\n至少，我们觉得是。事情一直很复杂。

column5: We may be walking into a trap.\nThis may all be part of The Triumvirate's plan.
column6: 我们可能正走进一个陷阱。\n这一切也许都在三人执政团的计划之中。

column5: Take their blade, feed it power, and then bring it back.\nThis may be what they've wanted all along. We've seen it.\nEverything we've done has only made their weapon stronger.
column6: 夺走他们的剑，喂养它力量，再把它送回去。\n这也许正是他们一直想要的。我们看出来了。\n我们所做的一切，只是让他们的武器变得更强。

column5: They let us steal their blade. They wanted it to happen.\nThey knew we'd bring it here, feed it death, and tap into the idol.\nBut not only that — we're bringing it right back to them, stronger than ever.
column6: 他们是故意让我们偷走那把剑的。这正是他们想要的。\n他们知道我们会把它带到这里，以死亡喂养它，并汲取灵像的力量。\n不仅如此——我们还会把它原样带回他们面前，比以往任何时候都更强。

column5: You may think we are wrong — that this is just a foolish theory.\nBut we must only look into the visions to realize the truth.\nThat, combined with some of your actions. Like clockwork.
column6: 你可能觉得我们错了——觉得这不过是无稽之谈。\n但只要我们去看那些幻象，就能明白真相。\n再加上你的一些举动。就像上了发条一样，分毫不差。

column5: It's almost like sometimes, you have no other choice.\nYou say or do things that push us down a certain path.\nBut more often than not, that path leads us to death.
column6: 有时候，你几乎像是别无选择。\n你说出或做出的事，会把我们推上某条道路。\n而那条路，往往通往死亡。

column5: How convenient then, that the blade feeds off of death.\nIn your hands, it has gotten more powerful than ever before.\nBut what force — what invisible hand — guides us down this path...?
column6: 那么，这把剑以死亡为食，又是多么方便啊。\n在你手中，它变得比以往任何时候都要强大。\n可究竟是什么力量——什么无形之手——在引导我们走上这条路……？

column5: It's quite simple, but we were always looking at it the wrong way.\nVenturing into Eastcrown, and seeing that ship, made us realize that.\nWhen we approached things from a different angle, it all made sense.
column6: 其实很简单，只是我们一直看错了方向。\n深入东冠，看到那艘船，让我们明白了这一点。\n当我们换个角度看问题时，一切就都说得通了。

column5: We've been struggling with visions of these “different” pasts.\nThey seemed to come out of nowhere, and complicate things.\nUntil recently, we only had to process visions of the future.
column6: 我们一直苦苦挣扎于那些“不同”过去的幻象。\n它们似乎凭空出现，把事情搅得一团乱。\n直到最近，我们要处理的还只是未来的幻象。

column5: He crosses his arms.
column6: 他抱起了双臂。

column5: At least, that's what we thought.
column6: 至少，我们当时是这么想的。

column5: I take a step forward, interested to see where he's going with this.
column6: 我上前一步，想知道他到底想说什么。

column5: But now we realize — we've never seen the future at all.\nIt's impossible to see what has not yet been written.\nBut it is easy to see what has already happened.
column6: 但现在我们明白了——我们从未见过未来。\n看见尚未被书写之物是不可能的。\n但看见已经发生的事，却很容易。

column5: Now he's lost me.
column6: 这下我听不懂了。

column5: These visions of different pasts aren't as out of place as we thought.\nYou were told you had visions of the future, and chose to believe that fact.\nBut they are not visions of the future. They too, are simply different pasts.
column6: 这些不同过去的幻象，并不像我们想的那么格格不入。\n有人告诉你那是未来的幻象，而你选择相信了这个说法。\n但它们不是未来的幻象。它们同样只是不同的过去。

column5: What...?
column6: 什么……？

column5: The key to all of this is The Blade of Exodus. It's a constant in every vision.\nBut the power within it varies, even when it shouldn't. There are... inconsistencies.\nEven if we have a vision of the same situation, the power inside the blade is different.
column6: 这一切的关键是流亡之刃。它在每个幻象中都是恒定的。\n但它蕴含的力量却会变化，哪怕本不该如此。存在着……矛盾之处。\n即便我们看到的是同一个情景的幻象，剑中的力量也不一样。

column5: The Triumvirate has some sort of dominion over time. That much is clear.\nThey possess the ability to grant their subjects eternal life. Like Ulrilc, and Sovy.\nWe need to operate under the assumption that this ability can be used in other ways.
column6: 三人执政团对时间有某种掌控力。这一点很清楚。\n他们拥有赐予臣属永恒生命的能力。比如乌尔里克，还有索维。\n我们必须假设这种能力还可以用在别的方面。

column5: He eyes the blade on my back.
column6: 他盯着我背上的剑。

column5: Mainly, in a way that could be used to strengthen The Blade of Exodus.\nThey could create a cycle — full of death and despair — that we are unable to break.\nWhen the cycle reaches an end, they could revert time, and gather that power all over again.
column6: 主要是，用来强化流亡之刃。\n他们可以制造一个轮回——充满死亡与绝望——让我们无法打破。\n当轮回走到尽头，他们便能逆转时间，将那份力量再次收集起来。

column5: The visions of the future you thought you were having? They aren't what you thought.\nWe believe they are visions of cycles in the past. Perhaps cycles where we have perished.\nDid your visions of the “future” involve your death in any way? Think about this, Monarch.
column6: 你以为你看到的那些未来幻象？它们并非你所想的那样。\n我们相信那是过去轮回的幻象。也许是我们在其中覆灭的轮回。\n你那些“未来”的幻象里，有没有以任何方式出现过你的死亡？好好想想，君主。

column5: Now that he mentions it, they did. I was stabbed by Sovy in the vision that started all of this.{w}\nAnd after touching the blade, my series of visions ended with me getting stabbed. That's odd.{w}\nI tell him these stories, and he smirks. It seems I'm only confirming his outlandish theories.
column6: 经他这么一提，确实有。在一切开始的那场幻象里，我被索维刺了一刀。{w}\n而触碰那把剑之后，我那一连串的幻象也以我被刺中告终。这很奇怪。{w}\n我把这些告诉他，他勾起嘴角。看来我只是在印证他那些荒诞的推论。

column5: Those were visions of past cycles, Monarch. Cycles where we failed.\nWhen we look at it like this, these different pasts make perfect sense.\nWe've been looking at them all wrong. That is — until just recently.
column6: 那些是过去轮回的幻象，君主。我们失败的轮回。\n这么一想，那些不同的过去就完全说得通了。\n我们一直看错了它们。直到——最近才明白。

column5: It seems that we retain some prior knowledge from these cycles.\nPerhaps that is why we act in certain ways, as if we have no options.\nIn the back of our mind, we're pushing ourselves in the same direction.
column6: 看来我们保留了一些来自那些轮回的旧有认知。\n也许正因如此，我们才会以某些方式行事，仿佛别无选择。\n在心底深处，我们一直把自己推向同一个方向。

column5: We think The Triumvirate is manipulating time.\nThey are doing this in order to make the blade even stronger.\nThe Occupation, the formation of The Rebellion, and the attack in the tunnels?
column6: 我们认为三人执政团在操纵时间。\n他们这么做，是为了让那把剑变得更强。\n占领、反抗军的成立，还有隧道里的那场袭击？

column5: All of those casualties simply served to give the blade more power.\nWe have no doubt that many will perish when we assault Balteus, as well.\nBut when the time comes, they can simply make it happen all over again.
column6: 那些伤亡，不过是用来给那把剑增添力量。\n我们毫不怀疑，进攻巴尔泰乌斯时也会有许多人丧命。\n但当那一刻到来，他们只需让一切重新来过。

column5: This is almost too much to comprehend.
column6: 这几乎让人难以理解。

column5: It makes sense, when you think about it. Especially with these tunnels.\nThose suits of armor knew exactly how to fortify this place for your army.\nThey must've retained their knowledge, and adapted each and every time.
column6: 仔细一想，确实有道理。尤其是这些隧道。\n那些铠甲士兵清楚地知道该如何为你的军队加固这个地方。\n他们必定保留了记忆，每一次都做出了调整。

column5: But only one question remains unanswered — why?\nWhy do they want to make this blade even stronger?\nWhat is their endgame? What do they desire...?
column6: 但只有一个问题还没有答案——为什么？\n他们为什么要让这把剑变得更强？\n他们的最终目的是什么？他们到底想要什么……？

column5: It is very possible that we are walking into a trap.\nThat is, unless, the blade has enough power to defeat them.\nTheir plan — if it's as I expect — is a double-edged sword.
column6: 我们很可能正走进一个陷阱。\n除非，这把剑拥有足以击败他们的力量。\n他们的计划——如果真如我所料——是一把双刃剑。

column5: An infinite cycle, created specifically to power the blade.\nThere must be a cycle — a “prime” cycle — where {i}we{/i} have the power to defeat them.\nA point where the blade is strong enough for us to win, but not yet strong enough for them.
column6: 一个无限的轮回，专门为给那把剑注入力量而被创造出来。\n必定存在一个轮回——一个“原初”轮回——在那里，{i}我们{/i}拥有击败他们的力量。\n一个剑的力量已足以让我们取胜，却还未强到足以让他们得逞的节点。

column5: All we can do is hope that we've reached that cycle.\nThe power in that blade is immense, but is it enough...?\nHopefully you understand what we are trying to say.
column6: 我们能做的，只有希望我们已经抵达了那个轮回。\n那把剑中的力量无比巨大，但是否足够……？\n希望你能明白我们想说什么。

column5: He's trying to tell me that we're trapped in some sort of time loop?{w}\nA loop that The Triumvirate fashioned in order to give the blade power...?{w}\nAnd not only that, but I never saw the future. I only saw failed past endeavors.
column6: 他是想告诉我，我们被困在某种时间循环里？{w}\n一个由三人执政团精心设计、用来给那把剑注入力量的循环……？{w}\n不仅如此，我从未看见过未来。我看到的只是过去失败的尝试。

column5: It's hard to believe, but death has definitely followed me and my allies.{w}\nIf their goal was to feed the blade with power, then they have certainly succeeded.{w}\nBut how far back does this cycle go? Could it reach as far back as The Occupation...?
column6: 很难相信，但死亡确实一直追随着我和我的同伴们。{w}\n如果他们的目的是以力量喂养那把剑，那他们无疑是成功了。{w}\n但这个轮回上溯到多久以前？会不会一直追到占领时期……？

column5: Wait a minute.
column6: 等等。

column5: Attack Mazeo, kill innocents, and incite a rebellion.{w}\nAttack that rebellion, provoke them into attacking your home, and then destroy them.{w}\nWith what Howl said — it almost does seem likely that we're walking into a trap. This can't be.
column6: 袭击马泽奥，杀害无辜者，挑起一场叛乱。{w}\n袭击那场叛乱，激他们进攻你的家园，然后将他们摧毁。{w}\n结合豪尔所说的话——我们似乎真的要走进一个陷阱了。这不可能。

column5: The reason we see these things is because of the energy within us.\nIt makes us sensitive, in a way that others are not. We are both special.\nBut I don't think visions are the only benefit of this power. There is more.
column6: 我们能看见这些东西，是因为我们体内的能量。\n它让我们以一种旁人没有的方式变得敏锐。我们两个都很特别。\n但我认为幻象并非这份力量唯一的好处。还有更多。

column5: Perhaps you see a flash of events that are happening elsewhere.\nPerhaps you can relive a conversation that has already happened.\nThese echoes of past cycles manifest themselves in many ways.
column6: 也许你会瞥见别处正在发生的事件。\n也许你能重温一段已经发生过的对话。\n过去轮回的这些回响，会以许多种方式显现。

column5: But when we look at it this way, everything makes sense.\nEverything has an explanation, and nothing is left up in the air.\nThe only question is — do you believe us? Do you think we are correct?
column6: 但这样看来，一切都说得通了。\n一切都有了解释，再没有悬而未决的事。\n唯一的问题是——你相信我们吗？你觉得我们说的对吗？

column5: Very well. It was enough to get this off our chest.\nWe only ask that you keep it in mind in the future.\nWhen we get to Balteus, things may become clear.
column6: 很好。能把这件事说出来，对我们来说就够了。\n我们只希望你在将来把它记在心里。\n等我们到了巴尔泰乌斯，事情或许会明朗起来。

column5: Good. We knew you would see the truth of things.\nThis was an impossible matter to discuss with anybody else.\nWe are special, and now we finally understand the reason why.
column6: 很好。我们就知道你会看清事情的真相。\n这件事无法和任何其他人谈论。\n我们很特别，而现在我们终于明白原因了。

column5: He turns to leave, but tilts his head back to address me one more time.{w}\nI guess he wanted to leave no stone unturned before our attack on Balteus.
column6: 他转身要走，却又回过头来，再一次对我开口。{w}\n我猜，他想在进攻巴尔泰乌斯之前把事情彻查清楚，不留死角。

column5: The Triumvirate is up to something — that much is clear.\nIf it aligns with our theory, at least you will be able to act.\nGetting caught off guard would damage us beyond repair.
column6: 三人执政团在谋划着什么——这一点很清楚。\n如果这与我们的推论吻合，至少你还能做出应对。\n被打个措手不及，会给我们造成无法挽回的损失。

column5: That is not something we want our Monarch to endure.\nBe prepared for anything, for the enemy will stop at nothing.\nIf you can do this, then perhaps our victory will be more likely.
column6: 那不是我们希望君主承受的事。\n做好万全准备，因为敌人会不择手段。\n如果你能做到这一点，也许我们获胜的希望就会更大。

column5: With that said, he sees himself out of my room.{w}\nThat all came out of nowhere, and I'm not sure how to react.{w}\nBut one thing was clear — there was so much we didn't know.
column6: 说完这些，他便自行离开了我房间。{w}\n这一切来得毫无预兆，我不知该如何反应。{w}\n但有一件事很清楚——我们不知道的事情太多了。

column5: But would we learn the truth in Balteus?{w}\nOr would we even make it that far? I don't know.{w}\nI start to feel uneasy, even with all this new knowledge.
column6: 但我们能在巴尔泰乌斯得知真相吗？{w}\n还是说，我们根本撑不到那里？我不知道。{w}\n即便知道了这些新东西，我仍开始感到不安。

column5: Could we really have been fundamentally wrong about everything?{w}\nAs I go about my business, it's impossible to shake that thought out of my head.
column6: 我们对一切的理解，难道真的从根本上就错了？{w}\n在我处理日常事务时，这个念头始终挥之不去。

column5: Sovy and his crew quickly made their way back to the docks.{w}\nHiding in the alleyway, much like before, they gathered their bearings.{w}\nThings hadn't gone according to plan — their true mission was a failure.
column6: 索维和他的手下迅速返回了码头。{w}\n他们像之前一样躲在巷子里，重新定了定神。{w}\n事情没有按计划发展——他们真正的任务失败了。

column5: What happened, Sovy?\nI thought you had everything under control.\nGet in — kill The Seer — and destroy the idol.
column6: 怎么回事，索维？\n我以为你把一切都掌控住了。\n潜进去——杀掉先知——毁掉灵像。

column5: What happened, Sovy?\nI thought you had everything under control.\nGet in — kill The Seeress — and destroy the idol.
column6: 怎么回事，索维？\n我以为你把一切都掌控住了。\n潜进去——杀掉先知——毁掉灵像。

column5: It's not that simple, Halin.\nI tried my best, and it wasn't a total failure.\nWe've dealt them a blow from which they'll never recover.
column6: 没那么简单，哈林。\n我已经尽力了，而且也不算全盘失败。\n我们给了他们一记永远无法恢复的打击。

column5: And you think The Triumvirate will be okay with that?\nThey don't tolerate failure. I'll get dragged into this, too.\nI don't want to suffer due to your inability to succeed, Sovy.
column6: 你以为三人执政团会对此满意？\n他们不容许失败。我也会被牵连进去。\n我不想因为你的无能而遭罪，索维。

column5: Let's not even mention The Blade of Exodus.\nYou just let them walk away with it...?\nI can't believe you were so foolish.
column6: 更别提流亡之刃了。\n你就那样让他们把它带走了……？\n我真不敢相信你会这么愚蠢。

column5: Don't worry. We'll get the job done.\nThey'll be happy enough with Damek out of the picture.\nIt'll buy us time while we formulate another plan, Halin.
column6: 别担心。我们会完成任务的。\n少了达梅克，他们就够满意了。\n这会为我们争取时间，让我们制定新的计划，哈林。

column5: If you're lucky enough to get another chance, you mean.\nYou'll need a pretty good excuse to get away with this.
column6: 你是说，如果你运气好还能有下一次机会的话。\n你得有个相当不错的借口才能蒙混过关。

column5: Sovy sighs, looking down at the ground.
column6: 索维叹了口气，低头看着地面。

column5: I hesitated, Halin.
column6: 我犹豫了，哈林。

column5: Hmm...?
I had him in my grasp, and I hesitated.\nThere was something in my head — saying not to kill him.\nThe same instinct I always listen to, and am {i}praised{/i} for.
column6: 他已经落在我手里了，我却犹豫了。\n我脑子里有个声音——叫我不要杀他。\n那正是我一直听从、并因此受到{i}称赞{/i}的直觉。

column5: That instinct has yet to let me down.\nI feel like he was meant to survive this battle.\nWe'll have more chances to kill him in the future.
column6: 那个直觉至今没有让我失望过。\n我觉得他本就注定要在这场战斗中活下来。\n将来我们还有更多机会杀他。

column5: Besides, with the condition I left him in, he'll be an easy target.\nNext time we cross paths, even a child could take him down.\nThis isn't as bad as you think, Halin. Today, we {i}won{/i}.
column6: 再说，我把他伤成那样，他会是个很容易得手的目标。\n下次我们再遇上，就连小孩都能放倒他。\n事情没你想的那么糟，哈林。今天，是我们{i}赢了{/i}。

column5: I had her in my grasp, and I hesitated.\nThere was something in my head — saying not to kill her.\nThe same instinct I always listen to, and am {i}praised{/i} for.
column6: 她已经落在我手里了，我却犹豫了。\n我脑子里有个声音——叫我不要杀她。\n那正是我一直听从、并因此受到{i}称赞{/i}的直觉。

column5: That instinct has yet to let me down.\nI feel like she was meant to survive this battle.\nWe'll have more chances to kill her in the future.
column6: 那个直觉至今没有让我失望过。\n我觉得她本就注定要在这场战斗中活下来。\n将来我们还有更多机会杀她。

column5: Besides, with the condition I left her in, she'll be an easy target.\nNext time we cross paths, even a child could take her down.\nThis isn't as bad as you think, Halin. Today, we {i}won{/i}.
column6: 再说，我把她伤成那样，她会是个很容易得手的目标。\n下次我们再遇上，就连小孩都能放倒她。\n事情没你想的那么糟，哈林。今天，是我们{i}赢了{/i}。

column5: For your sake, I hope they buy that excuse.
column6: 为了你好，我希望他们信你这套说辞。

column5: No, Halin. We must {i}never{/i} tell them the truth.\nTell them The Seer slipped through our grasp.\nI trust you to keep this silent for the time being.
column6: 不，哈林。我们{i}绝不能{/i}告诉他们真相。\n就说先知从我们手中逃脱了。\n这件事暂时就靠你保密了。

column5: No, Halin. We must {i}never{/i} tell them the truth.\nTell them The Seeress slipped through our grasp.\nI trust you to keep this silent for the time being.
column6: 不，哈林。我们{i}绝不能{/i}告诉他们真相。\n就说先知从我们手中逃脱了。\n这件事暂时就靠你保密了。

column5: You want me to {i}lie{/i} for you, now?
column6: 你现在是要我替你说{i}谎{/i}？

column5: It's for the best. Just trust me.\nI would do the same for you, Halin.\nTogether, we will acquire {i}any{/i} lost honor.
column6: 这是最好的办法。相信我。\n换作是你，我也会这么做，哈林。\n我们会一起把失去的荣誉{i}全部{/i}夺回来。

column5: Fine. But next time, I'll watch you.\nIf you can't finish the job — then I {i}will{/i}.\nThere's no place for hesitation in a time of war.
column6: 行。但下一次，我会盯着你。\n如果你下不了手——那就由我{i}来{/i}。\n战时容不得半点犹豫。

column5: Sovy nods, and Halin walks away.{w}\nThis leaves Sovy alone with Shane.
column6: 索维点点头，哈林转身离开。{w}\n码头上只剩下索维和肖恩。

column5: So, how are you feeling?
column6: 那么，你感觉怎么样？

column5: I'm fine.
column6: 我没事。

column5: You look conflicted.
column6: 你看起来心里很矛盾。

column5: I said I'm fine.
column6: 我说了我没事。

column5: Look. You killed Damek, Shane.\nI can understand what you're going through.
column6: 听着。你杀了达梅克，肖恩。\n我能理解你正在经历什么。

column5: Oh, can you?
column6: 哦，是吗？

column5: Yeah. I did the same thing in the past.\nBefore I joined The Triumvirate, I killed them all.\nLiars and cheaters deserve no less of a punishment.
column6: 是啊。我过去也做过同样的事。\n在加入三人执政团之前，我把他们全杀了。\n骗子和小人不配得到更轻的惩罚。

column5: He looked so sad, though...\nLike — how do I know what you said was true?\nA face can say a lot more than words ever can.
column6: 可他看起来那么悲伤……\n就像——我怎么知道你说的是真的？\n一张脸上的表情，能说的话远比言语更多。

column5: He was sad because he got caught, Shane.\nHe thought you were dead, so he didn't expect it.\nYou \"rose from the grave\" to deliver your vengeance.
column6: 他悲伤是因为他被抓住了，肖恩。\n他以为你已经死了，所以毫无防备。\n你“从坟墓里爬出来”来实施你的复仇。

column5: That is an opportunity he shall never have.\nHe didn't hesitate to send you to your death, remember?\nThere's no reason to give him a courtesy he never gave {i}you{/i}.
column6: 那是他永远得不到的机会。\n他毫不犹豫地把你送去送死，记得吗？\n没必要给他一份他从未给过{i}你{/i}的体面。

column5: Offering that olive branch is a good way to get yourself killed.\nThere's no going back now, Shane. You're one of us.\nAfter what you did, you're their enemy. For good.
column6: 递出那根橄榄枝，只会让你送命。\n现在没有回头路了，肖恩。你是我们的人了。\n在你做了那些事之后，你就是他们的敌人。永远都是。

column5: Hmm...?
Yes, but you are no longer an enemy of The Triumvirate.\nThey will sing your praise, and give you your every desire.\nThe victory of our battle was all thanks to you, Shane.
column6: 没错，但你不再是三人执政团的敌人了。\n他们会歌颂你，满足你的每一个愿望。\n我们这场战斗的胜利，全靠你，肖恩。

column5: I'm not sure how to feel...
column6: 我不知道该怎么想……

column5: Sometimes you need to act, rather than react.\nPush those feelings aside, and focus on survival.\nThere are many rebels who will seek you out for revenge.
column6: 有时候你需要主动行动，而不是被动反应。\n把那些感受抛到一边，专注于活下去。\n会有很多反抗军的人来找你报仇。

column5: And I expect you to show all of them the {i}same{/i} treatment.\nWelcome to The Inquisition, Shane. The {i}right{/i} side of history.
column6: 我希望你对他们所有人{i}一视同仁{/i}。\n欢迎加入审判庭，肖恩。站在历史{i}正确{/i}的一边。

column5: Sovy leads me to a boat, and takes me on a short voyage.{w}\nI have no idea where we're going, and our destination surprises me.{w}\nIt's not a place I've seen on any map, and looks unlike anything I've seen before.
column6: 索维带我上了船，走了一段短短的航程。{w}\n我完全不知道我们要去哪里，而目的地让我大吃一惊。{w}\n那是个我从未在任何地图上见过的地方，看起来也跟我以往见过的一切都不同。

column5: I follow behind him, unsure of where we'll even end up.{w}\nAfter a while, he turns to face me. I ask him for an explanation.{w}\nI trusted him enough to follow him here, but I had my limits.
column6: 我跟在他身后，连我们会到哪儿都心里没底。{w}\n过了一会儿，他转过身来面向我。我向他讨个说法。{w}\n我信任他，才跟到了这里，但我的信任也有限度。

column5: I know that we're almost at the end, [firstname].\nIt won't be much longer before we arrive on Baltean soil.\nSo it only makes sense that I show you where everything began.
column6: 我知道我们快到终点了，[firstname]。\n再过不久，我们就要踏上巴尔泰乌斯的土地了。\n所以，带你去看看一切开始的地方，也是顺理成章。

column5: He gestures broadly at everything behind him.
column6: 他朝身后的一切大手一挥。

column5: I come from this backwater town. Born and raised.\nIt was wiped off the map after all the villagers were murdered.\nGiven time, it might have even become the fifth nation of Alestia.
column6: 我出生在这个穷乡僻壤。生于此，长于此。\n在村民全被杀光之后，它就从地图上被抹去了。\n假以时日，它甚至可能成为阿莱斯提亚的第五个国家。

column5: But that was long ago, and nobody remembers this place.\nMy parents were in charge of the area. They were incredibly wealthy.\nThey had a force of men working the mines. Cheap labor — and big profits.
column6: 但那是很久以前的事了，没人记得这个地方。\n我的父母掌管着这片地区。他们富可敌国。\n他们有一批人在矿场干活。廉价的劳力——和丰厚的利润。

column5: It seems like Sovy was finally opening up to me.{w}\nThat was important. I needed to know that he could be trusted.{w}\nAnd if things went well, his loyalty to our cause would be confirmed.
column6: 看来索维终于对我敞开心扉了。{w}\n这很重要。我需要确定他是可以信任的。{w}\n如果一切顺利，他对我们事业的忠诚就能得到证实。

column5: As their son, they had me oversee all of this labor.\nIt was my job to make sure everybody hit their goals.\nI performed admirably, and put my foot down when needed.
column6: 作为他们的儿子，他们让我监管所有这些劳作。\n我的职责就是确保每个人都达成目标。\n我干得很出色，必要时也绝不手软。

column5: He walks toward a nearby house, and puts his hand on it.{w}\nTaking a loud breath, I can tell he's reliving unpleasant memories.
column6: 他走向附近的一栋房子，把手搭在上面。{w}\n他重重地吸了口气，我看得出他正在重温那些不快的记忆。

column5: Everything was going well, until the truth came out.\nThe people who raised me weren't my parents. Not even close.\nThey killed my parents while I was an infant, and took over this town.
column6: 一切都进展顺利，直到真相大白。\n养育我的人并不是我的父母。差得远了。\n在我还是个婴儿的时候，他们杀了我的父母，霸占了这座小镇。

column5: Raising me as their own, our relationship was built on a lie.\nI was serving killers, and usurpers. When I found out, I felt nothing but rage.\nThey stole this land — and the lives of its rightful rulers. Such an injustice.
column6: 他们把我当作亲生的养大，我们的关系却建立在谎言之上。\n我一直在侍奉凶手和篡位者。得知真相时，我心中只有愤怒。\n他们偷走了这片土地——还有它合法统治者们的性命。如此不公。

column5: The hand he was resting on the house slowly turns into a clenched fist.
column6: 他搭在房子上的那只手，慢慢握成了拳。

column5: I don't know what came over me, to be honest.\nI killed everybody. My so-called parents, and all the workers.\nI was lied to, by those who swore they loved me. I couldn't take it.
column6: 说实话，我不知道自己当时是怎么了。\n我把所有人都杀了。我所谓的父母，还有所有的工人。\n我被那些信誓旦旦说爱我的人欺骗了。我受不了。

column5: By rule of inheritance, in that moment — this town became mine.\nBut there was nobody else, and I was all by myself. I no longer wanted to live.\nI took myself to the cliff's edge, and thought about throwing myself into the ocean.
column6: 依照继承的规矩，就在那一刻——这座小镇归我了。\n但再无他人，只剩我孤身一人。我不想再活下去了。\n我走到悬崖边，想着纵身跳进大海。

column5: He turns back to face me, and I can see how sad he really is.
column6: 他转回身面对我，我看得出他究竟有多悲伤。

column5: That's when Ulric found me. He made sure I didn't do anything stupid.\nI don't know how he came across me when he did. I thought it could be providence.\nBut he saved me, and I told him everything. Instead of scolding me, he praised me.
column6: 就在这时，乌尔里克找到了我。他确保我没做出什么傻事。\n我不知道他怎么会那么巧遇上我。我以为那是天意。\n但他救了我，我把一切都告诉了他。他没有责备我，反而称赞了我。

column5: I was shocked. I expected to be dragged to the nearest prison.\nBut he took me right to The Triumvirate, and told them my story.\nThat's when they wanted me to become his Apprentice. I accepted.
column6: 我很震惊。我以为自己会被拖进最近的监狱。\n但他直接把我带到了三人执政团面前，讲了我的故事。\n就在那时，他们希望我成为他的学徒。我答应了。

column5: My desire for justice was something they wanted on their side.\nBut I no longer fought for my home village. I fought for all of Alestia.\nI swore an oath to them — that I would always fight for the rulers of this world.
column6: 他们对正义的渴望，正是他们想要拉拢的。\n但我不再为我的家乡而战。我为整个阿莱斯提亚而战。\n我向他们立下誓言——永远为这个世界的统治者而战。

column5: At the time, I believed it was them.\nBut learning the truth of The Monarchy? It just opened old wounds.\nI saw The Triumvirate in a new light — much like I saw my so-called parents.
column6: 当时，我相信统治者就是他们。\n但得知王室的真相？那只是揭开了旧伤。\n我用全新的眼光看待三人执政团——就像我看待我所谓的父母一样。

column5: Once more, the desire for justice rose to the forefront of my mind.\nYou may think my allegiance changed, and that it was a sudden shift — but it's not true.\nI've always fought for the same thing. It's just that sometimes, the tables need a little turning.
column6: 对正义的渴望，又一次涌上我心头。\n你可能觉得我的效忠变了，而且变得很突然——但事实并非如此。\n我一直都在为同一件事而战。只是有时候，形势需要一点扭转。

column5: He crosses his arms, and seems to be done talking for now.{w}\nHe leads me further into the village, and I follow — trusting him more.{w}\nWe eventually end up at a large building. One that served as the town hall.
column6: 他抱起双臂，看来暂时说完了。{w}\n他带我往村子深处走去，我跟在后面——对他多了几分信任。{w}\n我们最终来到一栋大建筑前。那是昔日的镇政厅。

column5: You may notice the bloodstains. \nBut don't worry. I threw all the bodies off a cliff with Ulric.\nYou won't be seeing anything gruesome, I can assure you.
column6: 你可能注意到了那些血迹。\n但别担心。我和乌尔里克把所有尸体都扔下悬崖了。\n我向你保证，你不会看到任何血腥的东西。

column5: What an odd way to put my mind at ease.
column6: 这安慰人的方式可真够奇怪的。

column5: This is where my parents lived. I was never really allowed in.\nI guess I should stop calling them my parents. They were more like captors.\nI longed to see the world, but I obeyed them out of a feeling of loyalty. I slaved away.
column6: 这是我父母住过的地方。我从没真正被允许进去过。\n我想我该别再叫他们父母了。他们更像是把我关起来的人。\n我渴望看看外面的世界，却出于一种忠诚感服从他们。我像奴隶一样干活。

column5: Sometimes I'd sneak into my Father's office and peel the stamps off of his letters.\nThey were incoming letters, so it's not like they had any use. I started to collect them.\nI stuck them to my bedroom wall and told myself that one day, I'd go and see those places.
column6: 有时我会溜进父亲的办公室，把他信件上的邮票揭下来。\n那些都是寄来的信，所以邮票本来也没什么用处。我开始收集它们。\n我把它们贴在我卧室的墙上，告诉自己总有一天要去看看那些地方。

column5: One day, I wanted to be free...
column6: 有一天，我渴望自由……

column5: He lets out a loud sigh.
column6: 他长叹一声。

column5: I thought I was free when The Triumvirate took me in.\nBut it turns out I just traded one form of bondage for another.\nShackles moved from my wrists, to my heart. I don't know which is worse.
column6: 三人执政团收留我时，我以为自己自由了。\n但结果我只是用一种束缚换来了另一种束缚。\n镣铐从我的手腕移到了我的心上。我不知道哪一种更糟。

column5: He holds a hand close to his heart.
column6: 他把一只手贴近心口。

column5: They pressed the blade against my chest, and gave me some of its power.\nIt allowed me to use it as my own, and gave me what they deemed “eternal life”.\nUlric grew to see this as an awful curse, but I embraced it; and to this day, I still do.
column6: 他们把剑按在我的胸口，给了我一部分它的力量。\n那让我能将它当作自己的武器使用，还给了我他们所谓的“永恒生命”。\n乌尔里克渐渐把这视为可怕的诅咒，我却欣然接受；直到今天，我依然如此。

column5: I see myself as a defender. I want to protect the reign of Alestia's true rulers.\nIf The Monarchy is restored to power, I will protect you, — and all of your descendants.\nYou have my word, and you know why I served the enemy. My virtue was simply misplaced.
column6: 我把自己看作一名守护者。我想守护阿莱斯提亚真正统治者的王权。\n如果王室重掌权力，我会保护你——以及你所有的后代。\n我说到做到，你也明白我为何曾为敌人效力。我的德行只是用错了地方。

column5: But now it rests with you. The true heir to the throne of Alestia.\nAnd that is where it shall remain, as long as I've proven my loyalty to you.\nKnowing everything that you do — do you trust me to protect you in battle?
column6: 但现在，它落在你身上。阿莱斯提亚王位的真正继承人。\n只要我向你证明了我的忠诚，它就会一直留在这里。\n既然你知道了这一切——你信得过我在战斗中保护你吗？

column5: Thank you very much, Monarch.\nI knew I picked the right way to tell you the truth.\nIf we did this anywhere else, it might've fallen flat.
column6: 非常感谢你，君主。\n我就知道，我选对了告诉你真相的方式。\n要是换个地方说，可能就毫无效果了。

column5: He smiles, and I can tell he's extremely relieved.
column6: 他笑了，我看得出他如释重负。

column5: I needed to get this off my chest before our attack on Balteus.\nNot knowing whether I had your trust — it was too much.\nWe're comrades now, though; and I'm no longer worried.
column6: 我需要在进攻巴尔泰乌斯之前把这件事说出来。\n不知道是否得到了你的信任——这让我难以承受。\n不过现在我们已是同伴了；我不再担心。

column5: With that, it seems like our business here is done.{w}\nThe choice to trust me with his past, and confide in me, meant a lot.{w}\nNone of my comrades had to carry their burdens alone. We were in this together.
column6: 就这样，我们在这里的事似乎结束了。{w}\n他选择信任我、把过去托付给我，这对我意义重大。{w}\n我的同伴们没有人需要独自背负重担。我们同舟共济。

column5: Very well. I respect your choice, Monarch.\nAs wrong as it is — it is your mistake to make.\nI can't say I didn't try to win you over. I really did.
column6: 好吧。我尊重你的选择，君主。\n无论这有多么错误——那也是你该犯的错。\n我不能说自己没有试着争取过你。我确实试过。

column5: He lets out a loud sigh, and his shoulders slump down.
column6: 他长叹一声，肩膀垂了下来。

column5: Promise that you'll keep this between us.\nI wouldn't want anybody to... start talking.\nJust do that — and I promise to keep to myself.
column6: 答应我，这件事只留在我们之间。\n我不想让任何人……开始议论。\n你只要这么做——我就答应管好自己。

column5: I nod, agreeing.{w}\nHe confided in me, and I respected that.{w}\nBut as far as trust went, I was still skeptical.
column6: 我点头应允。{w}\n他向我吐露了心事，我尊重这一点。{w}\n但说到信任，我仍持怀疑态度。

column5: Let's get back to Mazeo, alright?\nI'm sure there's lots to do before the end.\nThanks for joining me, but I think we need to leave.
column6: 我们回马泽奥吧，好吗？\n我相信在终局之前还有很多事要做。\n谢谢你陪我来这一趟，但我想我们该走了。

column5: We start walking back the way we came, and head to our boat.{w}\nThis place was wiped off the map — I had no idea that it existed.{w}\nIt makes me wonder just what else this world could be hiding.
column6: 我们沿着来路往回走，朝我们的船去。{w}\n这个地方从地图上被抹去了——我根本不知道它还存在。{w}\n这让我不禁去想，这个世界还藏着多少别的东西。

column5: Before we get on the boat, I look back at the town, one last time.{w}\nAfter the war was over, maybe we could rebuid this place, and grow it.{w}\nA new nation, with new rules. If we had the opportunity, we should seize it.
column6: 上船之前，我最后回头看了一眼那座小镇。{w}\n等战争结束后，也许我们可以重建这里，让它发展壮大。{w}\n一个全新的国家，全新的规则。如果我们有机会，就该抓住它。

column5: We start to sail away, and leave this place behind us for now.{w}\nBut I know Sovy better than I did before, and that could only bring good.
column6: 我们启航离去，暂时把这里抛在身后。{w}\n但我比以前更了解索维了，这只会是好事。

column5: He was carrying a weight on his shoulders, and it was no longer there.
column6: 他肩上曾背负着沉重的负担，如今已不复存在。

column5: As soon as we enter the town square, Ulric motions for all of us to stay close.{w}\nPeople run amok, while others try to peddle their wares, waving us over.{w}\nIt almost seems just like Mazeo, but the products must be different.
column6: 我们一走进城镇广场，乌尔里克就打手势让我们都跟紧些。{w}\n人们四处奔走，另一些人则兜售着货物，朝我们挥手招呼。{w}\n这里几乎跟马泽奥一模一样，只是货物想必不同。

column5: Good, the tavern is in the same place.\nIt's just over there, so we'll make it on time.
column6: 很好，酒馆还在老地方。\n就在那边，我们能准时赶到。

column5: He crosses his arms, and looks around the town square.{w}\nThen, he rubs his arm in a way that almost hides his tattoo.{w}\nBut it's too late. I can already see the townspeople staring.
column6: 他抱起双臂，环顾着城镇广场。{w}\n接着，他揉着手臂，动作几乎遮住了他的纹身。{w}\n但已经太迟了。我已经看到镇民们在盯着看。

column5: Ulric was definitely hiding something from all of us.{w}\nI'd hate to say he's losing our trust, but he's definitely suspicious.{w}\nNothing he's told me adds up with what the Alarinthians have said.
column6: 乌尔里克肯定对我们所有人隐瞒了什么。{w}\n我不想说他在失去我们的信任，但他确实很可疑。{w}\n他告诉我的话，和阿拉林西亚人所说的完全对不上。

column5: Almost out of fear, it seems that the townspeople avoid us.{w}\nEye contact is as far as we go, leaving us lots of room to maneuver.{w}\nI guess that helps. It'd suck if they all invaded our personal bubble.
column6: 镇民们似乎在恐惧之下躲着我们。{w}\n最多只是对视一眼，给我们留出了充足的活动空间。{w}\n我想这样也好。要是他们全挤进我们的私人空间，那才叫难受。

column5: Let's not waste too much time out here, alright?\nI think we only have a few hours until the ball begins.\nI'll stay here, but feel free to look around for a bit.
column6: 我们别在外面浪费太多时间，好吗？\n我想距离舞会开始只剩几个小时了。\n我会待在这儿，不过你们可以随便逛逛。

column5: Honestly, I expected Alarinthia to be different.{w}\nBut it looks like I'm staring at an alternate version of Mazeo.{w}\nThe only thing that stands out is the architecture, and the heat.
column6: 说实话，我本以为阿拉林西亚会不一样。{w}\n但看来我盯着的不过是另一个版本的马泽奥。{w}\n唯一突出的东西是建筑风格，还有那股热浪。

column5: That heat...
column6: 那股热浪……

column5: It didn't change one bit when we got to the city.{w}\nHowever, the natives seem used to it, walking around with ease.{w}\nMost of them aren't fully clothed, wearing a getup much like Ulric's.
column6: 进了城之后，它一点也没减弱。{w}\n不过当地人似乎习以为常，走起路来从容自在。{w}\n他们大多穿得不多，打扮和乌尔里克差不多。

column5: I guess it's my fault for expecting something different out of this place.{w}\nBefore we head to the tavern, I decide to look around for a few minutes.{w}\nMaybe it would be a good idea to talk to Ulric as well. He's acting strange.
column6: 我猜是我自己不对，不该指望这地方能有什么不同。{w}\n去酒馆之前，我决定先四处看看几分钟。{w}\n也许顺便和乌尔里克谈谈是个好主意。他举止很反常。

column5: It's a book about Sixers — criminals in Alarinthia's past.
column6: 这是一本关于“六人帮”的书——阿拉林西亚历史上的罪犯。

column5: I look through the market stalls. There's a few books on display.{w}\nThere's one about \"Sixers\", so I figure I should give it a read.{w}\nThat term has been thrown around recently, and I wanted to learn more.
column6: 我翻了翻市场摊位。上面摆着几本书。{w}\n其中一本是关于“六人帮”的，我想我该读一读。{w}\n这个词最近常被提起，我想多了解一些。

column5: It's a book about Draycu's reign over Alarinthia.
column6: 这是一本关于德雷库统治阿拉林西亚的书。

column5: On top of the crates, rests a book about Draycu's reign.{w}\nPerhaps some young Alarinthians were reading up on him before the ball.{w}\nIt definitely paints a grim picture of the nation. Draycu must be very strong.
column6: 箱子上放着一本关于德雷库统治的书。{w}\n也许有些年轻的阿拉林西亚人在舞会前研读他。{w}\n它确实把这个国家描绘得一派阴森。德雷库一定非常强大。

column5: Hey.
column6: 嘿。

column5: I have no idea, but it doesn't really matter.\nI'm pretty sure that we could handle whatever they throw at us.\nBut if he truly {i}does{/i} work for Vivien, then we have some good luck.
column6: 我不知道，但那也不重要。\n我很确定，不管他们扔给我们什么，我们都能应付。\n但如果他{i}真的{/i}为薇薇安效力，那我们的运气还不错。

column5: We could use some of that, couldn't we?\nSo for now, I'm going to believe Drakeor. But only for now.\nIf anything seems suspicious at the tavern, I'll tip you off.
column6: 我们正需要点好运，不是吗？\n所以眼下，我打算相信德雷克。但只是眼下。\n如果在酒馆里发现任何可疑之处，我会给你通风报信。

column5: Although, the prospect of a tavern brawl does sound appealing.\nYou haven't seen true fighting until you've seen it in Alarinthia.\nJust thinking about it gets my blood boiling. It's been too long.
column6: 不过，酒馆斗殴这种事听起来倒是挺诱人的。\n你只有在阿拉林西亚见过打斗，才算见识过真正的战斗。\n光是想想就让我热血沸腾。已经太久了。

column5: Of course, I'll try my best to keep our visit a peaceful one.\nI don't want to end up fighting for our freedom in the coliseum.\nTheir methods of punishing prisoners are still pretty harsh.
column6: 当然，我会尽力让我们这趟行程平安无事。\n我可不想最后在竞技场里为自由而战。\n他们惩罚囚犯的手段还是相当残酷。

column5: I hate to talk about this, so I'll try making it quick.\nVivien obviously isn't the first person to rebel against Alarinthia's laws.\nThe first one, at least in recorded history, was named Ulric — like me.
column6: 我不喜欢谈这个，所以尽量长话短说。\n薇薇安显然不是第一个反抗阿拉林西亚法律的人。\n至少在有记载的历史上，第一个反抗的人叫乌尔里克——和我同名。

column5: Many people followed after his ideals, including my parents.\nSo much so, that they decided to name me after him. I don't like it.\nThat's all it is, really. My name is a silly little tribute.
column6: 许多人追随他的理想，包括我的父母。\n他们甚至因此决定用他的名字给我命名。我不喜欢这样。\n真的就是这么回事。我的名字不过是种傻气的致敬。

column5: I guess it doesn't help that I also actually look like him.\nOr at least, all artistic and textual descriptions of him.\nA pretty cool coincidence, but that's all it is.
column6: 我想，我自己还真长得像他，这也让事情更糟。\n或者至少，像所有关于他的绘画和文字描述。\n很酷的巧合，但也仅此而已。

column5: I knew this stuff would come up as soon as we got here.\nJust remember, you've known me long before this trip.\nDon't come to judge me by the things these people say.
column6: 我就知道一到这儿，这些事就会被翻出来。\n记住，你在这趟旅程之前早就认识我了。\n别因为这些人的话就来评判我。

column5: I'd rather not talk about that, right now.\nBut I have a feeling you'll find out soon enough.\nIt's complicated, and we're really short on time.
column6: 我现在不太想谈这个。\n但我觉得你很快就会知道的。\n事情很复杂，而且我们时间真的不多。

column5: Just trust me, alright? It's nothing bad.\nI earned these — they weren't ripped off.\nLet's grab a drink in the tavern and chat.
column6: 相信我就好，行吗？不是什么坏事。\n这些是我挣来的——不是抢来的。\n我们去酒馆喝一杯，聊一聊。

column5: That's none of your business. Not yet.\nAgain, just trust me, okay...? Please.\nThere's lots going on that you don't know.
column6: 那不关你的事。至少现在还不关。\n再说一次，相信我就好，行吗……？拜托。\n有很多事你都不知道。

column5: That's not to say that you'll never know it.\nJust sit back and wait until the time is right.\nI promise that everything will make sense soon.
column6: 我不是说你永远不会知道。\n你只管安心等着，等到时机合适。\n我保证，很快一切就都会说得通了。

column5: Other than the tavern, not really.\nThere's just the market stalls, like Mazeo.\nHowever, there's no laws in place for this stuff.
column6: 除了酒馆，还真没什么。\n只有像马泽奥那样的市场摊位。\n不过，这些东西在这里没有法律管制。

column5: You can buy whatever you want in Alarinthia.\nPirates make a living bringing illicit goods overseas.\nSo whatever your heart desires, you can probably find.
column6: 在阿拉林西亚，你想买什么都能买到。\n海盗靠把违禁品运到海外为生。\n所以你心里想要的东西，大概都能找到。

column5: But I don't think you're the type of person to want that stuff.\nSo if it's all the same to you, we should probably get to the tavern.\nRemember, we're on a bit of a schedule. Our time is valuable.
column6: 但我觉得你不是会想要那种东西的人。\n所以如果你不介意，我们该去酒馆了。\n记住，我们的行程有点紧。时间宝贵。

column5: There's tons of vases and jars full of whatever product people are peddling.{w}\nFortaime inspects them with a curiosity that I almost can't describe.{w}\nHowever, Ulric is pretty quick to put that curiosity to an end.
column6: 那里堆满了花瓶和罐子，装满了人们兜售的各种货品。{w}\n福泰姆带着一种我几乎无法形容的好奇心打量着它们。{w}\n不过，乌尔里克很快就终结了那份好奇。

column5: Hey, cut that out.\nYou have no idea what's in there.\nIt could be drugs, or illegal weapons.
column6: 嘿，别碰那个。\n你根本不知道里面装着什么。\n可能是毒品，或是非法武器。

column5: There are illegal weapons...?
column6: 还有非法武器……？

column5: Oh, of course. You have to improvise around here.\nYour goal is to always be stronger than everyone else.\nThat requires some creativity, especially in weapon design.
column6: 哦，当然。在这地方你得随机应变。\n你的目标就是永远比所有人都强。\n那需要一些创造力，尤其是在武器设计上。

column5: The greatsword even originated in Alarinthia.\nYou don't see many people carrying them on the mainland.\nI was raised with it, though — so I can't use anything else.
column6: 巨剑甚至就起源于阿拉林西亚。\n在大陆上，你很少见到有人带着它。\n不过我从小就用它——所以别的武器我都用不惯。

column5: Whoa, that's pretty cool.\nI wonder what I can find, then!
column6: 哇，那可真酷。\n那我想想我能找到些什么！

column5: What part of illegal don't you understand?\nThere are laws in place to prevent more inhumane creations.\nBut those laws fail to reach places like the town square markets.
column6: “非法”两个字你哪部分听不懂？\n是有法律来防止制造更不人道的东西。\n但那些法律管不到像城镇广场集市这样的地方。

column5: You could touch something laced with poison, or worse.\nJust keep your hands off of this stuff and stay close to me.\nAlways assume that everything here is out to get you.
column6: 你可能碰到涂了毒的东西，或者更糟的。\n别碰这些东西，跟紧我。\n永远假设这里的一切都想害你。

column5: Wow, you make this place sound so luxurious.\nBut alright. I'll do what you say — for now.
column6: 哇，你把这里说得可真是奢华。\n不过好吧。我照你说的做——暂时。

column5: People run around the town square, clearly on a mission.{w}\nIt's more chaotic than Mazeo, and that's definitely saying something.{w}\nValessa stands there, watching everybody intently. She seems very interested.
column6: 人们在城镇广场上四处奔忙，显然各有要事。{w}\n这里比马泽奥还要混乱，这可不是随便说说的。{w}\n瓦莱莎站在那里，专注地看着每一个人。她似乎非常感兴趣。

column5: Is this place always so busy?
column6: 这地方总是这么忙碌吗？

column5: Yeah. It can even get worse.\nThe busy hours are closer to night time.\nBut not tonight, with the ball and all.
column6: 是啊。有时候还会更糟。\n最忙的时段接近夜晚。\n但今晚不会，毕竟有舞会。

column5: Do people live in their market stalls, like Mazeo?
column6: 人们像在马泽奥一样，住在自己的摊位里吗？

column5: No, not really. They get enough business to have their own homes.\nIt's actually the opposite here. Running a stall is a sign of wealth.
column6: 不，基本上不是。他们生意够好，都有自己的家。\n在这里其实正相反。经营摊位是财富的象征。

column5: So the more you work, the more money you make.\nSee, that actually makes sense. Don't you think?
column6: 所以你干得越多，赚的钱就越多。\n你看，这其实挺有道理的。你不觉得吗？

column5: Yeah, but it doesn't make up for the other shortcomings.\nThe markets are busy, and unsafe. People die all the time.\nIt's a cutthroat culture here, so you're always in danger.
column6: 是啊，但这弥补不了其他缺点。\n市场又忙又危险。总是有人丧命。\n这里的风气残酷无情，所以你永远身处险境。

column5: If I could choose a place to open up shop, I'd choose Mazeo.\nIt might be harder, and less profitable, but it'd be safe.\nYou wouldn't get caught up in other people's fights.
column6: 如果让我选个地方开店，我会选马泽奥。\n可能更难，利润也更少，但至少安全。\n你不会被卷进别人的争斗里。

column5: That happens here?
column6: 这里会发生那种事？

column5: All the time. It's almost unavoidable.\nYou can't turn around without bumping into anybody here.\nIt gets worse the deeper you go. But we won't go that deep.
column6: 经常发生。几乎无法避免。\n在这儿，你一转身都会撞到人。\n越往深处越糟。不过我们不会去那么深。

column5: Of course, the flowing of alcohol doesn't make things easier.\nPeople are always rowdy, looking for some fun, or a fight.\nYou also wouldn't be able to get some peace and quiet.
column6: 当然，酒水畅流也让事情更难办。\n人们总是吵吵嚷嚷，寻欢作乐，或者找架打。\n你也别想得到片刻安宁。

column5: Alright, alright — you win.\nWhy do so many people do it then?\nI mean, set up shop, and put up with that?
column6: 好吧好吧——你赢了。\n那为什么还有这么多人做这行？\n我是说，开店，还要忍受这些？

column5: Probably because they don't know anything else.\nGetting to the mainland is the last thing on their minds.\nWherever you grow up, that's what \"normal\" is to you.
column6: 大概是因为他们不知道别的生活方式。\n去大陆是他们最不关心的事。\n你在哪里长大，那里对你来说就是“正常”。

column5: I guess that makes sense.\nValinorth is normal to me, and Mazeo is weird.\nBut I bet it'd be the other way around for Damek.
column6: 我想这说得通。\n瓦利诺斯对我来说是正常的，马泽奥就很古怪。\n但我打赌对达梅克来说正好相反。

column5: Exactly.
column6: 正是如此。

column5: I make my way to the docks, happy to see that almost everybody else has done the same.{w}\nOur forces line the entire area. Dozens of ships are ours to command. We stand a real chance.{w}\nMaking my way down the docks, I notice all of our forces talking amongst themselves.
column6: 我朝码头走去，很高兴看到几乎其他所有人都已经到了。{w}\n我们的部队排满了整片区域。数十艘船归我们调遣。我们真的有机会。{w}\n一路走过码头，我注意到我们的部队都在彼此交谈。

column5: This is the unity that our world needed. The unity that we're fighting for.{w}\nThough not everybody saw eye-to-eye, they could all co-exist with one another.{w}\nThere would be no more oppression for those who thought differently than our rulers.
column6: 这就是我们的世界所需要的团结。我们为之奋斗的团结。{w}\n尽管并非所有人意见一致，他们却能彼此共存。{w}\n再也不会有因为想法与统治者不同而遭受的压迫。

column5: That is, of course — if we won.
column6: 当然——前提是我们赢了。

column5: Mylus is nowhere to be seen, but somehow I'm not surprised.{w}\nHe came to Alarinthia and back, and for that I was grateful.{w}\nIt was time for him to rest, and focus on what to do next.
column6: 哪里都看不到迈勒斯，但我不知为何并不意外。{w}\n他跟着去了阿拉林西亚又回来，为此我心怀感激。{w}\n该让他休息了，专注于下一步该怎么做。

column5: I notice Sovy helping our forces load supplies onto the boats.{w}\nThe gamble of letting him join our side seems to be paying off.{w}\nI'm certain his help would be invaluable as we entered Balteus.
column6: 我注意到索维在帮我们的部队把物资搬上船。{w}\n让他加入我们这一方的这场赌注，看来正在得到回报。{w}\n我确信，在我们进入巴尔泰乌斯时，他的帮助将无比宝贵。

column5: Staying true to his word, Sovy was nowhere to be seen.{w}\nIt's probably for the best. Letting him help us was too risky.{w}\nBut part of me wonders if I'd ever see him again after this.
column6: 索维信守诺言，哪里都见不到他。{w}\n这大概是最好的结果。让他帮我们太冒险了。{w}\n但我心里有一部分在想，这之后我还会不会再见到他。

column5: As I continue down the docks, eyes start to fixate on me.{w}\nNot just me, but the blade upon my back as well. They all knew who I was.{w}\nAt this moment, I feel the weight resting on my shoulders — but I stand strong.
column6: 我继续沿着码头走着，目光开始聚集在我身上。{w}\n不只是我，还有我背上的那把剑。他们都知道我是谁。{w}\n此刻，我感受到肩上的重担——但我依然挺立。

column5: This was a burden that I was ready to carry.{w}\nNo — this was a burden that I was {i}born{/i} to carry.{w}\nI smile at them as I walk by, and they do so in turn.
column6: 这是我准备好背负的重担。{w}\n不——这是我{i}生来{/i}就要背负的重担。{w}\n走过时我对他们微笑，他们也报以微笑。

column5: As I walk, I eventually run into Damek.{w}\nHe's overseeing everybody's efforts — making sure it goes smoothly.{w}\nThere was a lot to transport. We'd all need weapons, food, and drink.
column6: 走着走着，我最终遇到了达梅克。{w}\n他正监督着所有人的工作——确保一切顺利进行。{w}\n要运送的东西很多。我们都需要武器、食物和饮水。

column5: Quite the army, isn't it?\nSalus would be proud. I know he would.\nForgive me for taking charge, though. You deserve a break.
column6: 真是支了不起的军队，不是吗？\n萨卢斯会为你骄傲的。我知道他一定会的。\n不过，原谅我擅自担起了指挥。你该歇一歇了。

column5: Or at least, a chance to save your energy.\nYou'll need most of it in Balteus — not here.\nWe'll take care of everything until then.
column6: 或者至少，是个节省精力的机会。\n你的精力大部分要留到巴尔泰乌斯——不是用在这里。\n在那之前，一切交给我们。

column5: I nod, thankful that Damek is taking the initiative.{w}\nI'd definitely need to use the voyage as time to prepare.{w}\nMy skill with this blade is limited, but I know I can improve.
column6: 我点点头，感谢达梅克主动担起这些。{w}\n我肯定需要利用这段航程来做好准备。{w}\n我用这把剑的水平有限，但我知道自己可以进步。

column5: I made sure to put us on the same boat as each other.\nEveryone, actually. Howl, Valessa, Fortaime, Ulric, Pro...\nIt's probably best if we're all together for the end of this journey.
column6: 我特意把我们安排在了一条船上。\n其实是所有人。豪尔、瓦莱莎、福泰姆、乌尔里克、普洛……\n这段旅程的终点，我们最好都在一起。

column5: That much was true. I'd need my friends by my side for this.{w}\nWe were about to change the entire world. We'd be slaying \"Gods\".{w}\nPart of me wonders just who they are — and why they do what they've done.
column6: 这话不假。这件事我需要朋友们在我身边。{w}\n我们即将改变整个世界。我们要弑杀“神明”。{w}\n我心中有一部分在想，他们究竟是谁——又为何要做这些事。

column5: There's probably no point in concerning myself with that information.{w}\nNothing about them could excuse what they've done. They need to fall.{w}\nI thank Damek for everything that he's done, and this makes him happy.
column6: 去纠结这些信息大概也没什么意义。{w}\n他们的一切都无法为他们所做的事开脱。他们必须倒下。{w}\n我感谢达梅克所做的一切，这让他很高兴。

column5: Of course, [firstname]. Anything to help you out.\nBut I think we're almost ready to set sail. Want to get on board?\nMight as well lead by example. A lot of people are just standing around.
column6: 当然，[firstname]。只要能帮上你。\n不过我想我们差不多可以启航了。要上船吗？\n不妨以身作则。很多人还只是站在那儿。

column5: We turn to leave, but we're quickly interrupted.{w}\nIt's the last person I'd expect to see, but I'm not surprised.
column6: 我们转身要走，却很快被打断了。{w}\n那是我最意想不到会见到的人，但我并不意外。

column5: Leaving without me, Damek?\nI thought you wanted me to come along.
column6: 达梅克，你要丢下我就走？\n我还以为你想让我一起去的。

column5: Hey Gryz, happy to see you.\nWe weren't leaving — just getting on board.\nHopefully everybody else will take the hint and follow suit.
column6: 嘿，格瑞兹，很高兴见到你。\n我们不是要走——只是先上船而已。\n希望其他人也能明白过来，跟着照做。

column5: Fair enough. Hey there, [firstname].\nDamek told me everything when you got back from Alarinthia.\nIt seems like we were looking at things the wrong way all along.
column6: 那倒是。你好啊，[firstname]。\n你们从阿拉林西亚回来时，达梅克把一切都告诉我了。\n看来我们一直都用错了眼光看事情。

column5: At least, I definitely was.\nI thought that my death in those tunnels would redeem me.\nBut now I know that my fate lies elsewhere — in Balteus.
column6: 至少，我肯定是错了。\n我以为在那些隧道里死去就能赎罪。\n但现在我知道，我的命运在别处——在巴尔泰乌斯。

column5: I'm glad that his outlook has changed.{w}\nI couldn't let him kill himself back in our HQ.{w}\nHe was just lost — and needed some direction.
column6: 我很高兴他的想法改变了。{w}\n我不能让他在我们总部里自杀。{w}\n他只是迷失了——需要有人给他指个方向。

column5: At first, I was furious that you denied me my redemption.\nBut when Damek came to see me, I looked at it differently.\nI was meant to survive those tunnels, and help your final attack.
column6: 起初，你拒绝了我的赎罪，我很愤怒。\n但当达梅克来看我时，我换了个角度看这件事。\n我本就该在那些隧道里活下来，帮你完成最后的进攻。

column5: He holds out his hand, awaiting my response.
column6: 他伸出手，等着我的回应。

column5: What do you say...? \n\"To The Triumvirate's fall\"?\nMazeo can rest with Lillith for now.
column6: 你觉得呢……？\n“敬三人执政团的覆灭”？\n马泽奥暂且可以和莉莉丝安息了。

column5: Yeah — to The Triumvirate's fall.{w}\nI shake his hand, and his grip is firm.{w}\nThe support our cause is getting overwhelms me.
column6: 好——敬三人执政团的覆灭。{w}\n我握住他的手，他的手掌很有力。{w}\n我们的事业得到的支持让我感到心潮澎湃。

column5: Thank you, Monarch. Let's put the past behind us.\nHonestly, I think all of us want to forget about those tunnels.\nI promise that from here on out, I'll maintain a clear mind.
column6: 谢谢你，君主。让我们把过去抛在身后。\n说实话，我想我们所有人都想忘掉那些隧道里的事。\n我保证，从现在起，我会保持清醒的头脑。

column5: I nod, and we start making our way toward the boat.{w}\nOur vessel is the same one we used to get to Alarinthia.{w}\nIt's a bit bigger than the rest, and would work as a mobile HQ.
column6: 我点点头，我们开始朝船走去。{w}\n我们的船就是之前去阿拉林西亚时用的那一艘。{w}\n它比其余的稍大一些，可以当作移动的总部。

column5: When I get to the deck, I turn around and look at the docks.{w}\nEveryone is saying their final goodbyes, since we might not make it back.{w}\nI give them all the time they need, and slowly watch as they board our fleet.
column6: 我走上甲板，回身望向码头。{w}\n每个人都在做着最后的告别，因为我们也许回不来了。{w}\n我给他们留出需要的时间，静静看着他们登上我们的船队。

column5: Actually, I might not make it back either. That thought fills me with fright.{w}\nTaking one last look at Mazean soil, I say goodbye under my breath.{w}\nWhat happened next, would change the course of Alestian history forever.
column6: 其实，我也许也回不来了。这个念头让我满心恐惧。{w}\n最后望了一眼马泽奥的土地，我低声作了道别。{w}\n接下来发生的事，将永远改变阿莱斯提亚历史的走向。

column5: We find this army quite impressive.\nSo many people are willing to fight for our cause.\nLet us hope that the rest of the world accepts your rule.
column6: 我们觉得这支军队相当了不起。\n这么多人都愿意为我们的事业而战。\n但愿世界的其他地方也能接受你的统治。

column5: I nod. That would be our next challenge.{w}\nThey wouldn't just bow to new rulers overnight.{w}\nIt'd take serious effort, coordination, and planning.
column6: 我点点头。那将是我们接下来的挑战。{w}\n他们不会一夜之间就向新统治者臣服。{w}\n那需要付出巨大的努力、协调与谋划。

column5: We thought you deserved a break, so we took action.\nYour energy is best conserved until we reach Balteus.\nYou needn't worry about stocking or manning the ships.
column6: 我们觉得你该歇一歇，所以就动手了。\n你的精力最好留到我们抵达巴尔泰乌斯之前。\n你不必操心物资补给或船上的人手。

column5: I smile, thankful that Howl is taking the initiative.{w}\nI'd definitely need to use the voyage as time to prepare.{w}\nI wasn't as skilled with this blade as I could be. I needed to practice.
column6: 我笑了，感谢豪尔主动担起这些。{w}\n我肯定需要利用这段航程来做好准备。{w}\n我用这把剑的技艺还不到家。我需要练习。

column5: By the way, we made sure that we're all on the same boat.\nYou and your cloest comrades, together in these final moments.\nWe thought it fitting, since this is the end of our long journey.
column6: 顺便一提，我们确保大家都在这同一条船上。\n你和最亲密的同伴们，在这最后的时刻聚在一起。\n我们觉得这样很合适，毕竟这是我们漫长旅程的终点。

column5: Yeah, having my friends close by would be a big help.{w}\nThis was a stressful time, and my comrades gave me a sense of comfort.{w}\nThere's no other group of people I'd rather have by my side as we reached the end.
column6: 是啊，有朋友们在身边会是很大的帮助。{w}\n这段时间压力很大，我的同伴们给了我一种安慰。{w}\n在走到终点时，我身边最想有的就是他们。

column5: We think it may be time to board the ship, [firstname].\nLeading by example is a good idea. Too many people just standing around.\nIf we show that we're ready to leave — they might take it as a sign to hurry up.
column6: 我们觉得也许该上船了，[firstname]。\n以身作则是好主意。太多人只是站在那儿。\n如果我们表明已经准备好了——他们也许就会当作该抓紧的信号。

column5: We turn to leave, but we're quickly interrupted.{w}\nIt's the last person I'd expect to see, but I'm not surprised.
column6: 我们转身要走，却很快被打断了。{w}\n那是我最意想不到会见到的人，但我并不意外。

column5: Hey, now — don't leave without me.\nOr at least, let me say a few words before you do.\nI've been thinking a lot since we last met in those tunnels.
column6: 嘿，等等——别丢下我就走。\n或者至少，在你们走之前让我说几句。\n自从我们在那些隧道里最后一次见面后，我想了很多。

column5: Gryz stands before us with a smile on his face.{w}\nIt's good to see him again. I was curious about what happened to him.{w}\nI figured he ran away, since he almost disappeared — but I'm glad that he's back.
column6: 格瑞兹面带微笑站在我们面前。{w}\n很高兴再见到他。我一直好奇他后来怎么样了。{w}\n我以为他逃走了，因为他几乎消失了——但我很高兴他回来了。

column5: We know this one. He was there by the idol.\nBlinded by his quest for redemption, if we're not mistaken.\nIt is unlikely that he knows the truth of what's going on, here.
column6: 我们认识这个人。他当时就在灵像旁。\n如果我们没记错，他被赎罪的执念蒙蔽了双眼。\n他不太可能知道这里正在发生的真相。

column5: Of course I do. I know about The Monarchy, as well. \nDamek told me everything when you got back from Alarinthia.\nIt turns out that we were all looking at things the wrong way.
column6: 我当然知道。我也知道王室的事。\n你们从阿拉林西亚回来时，达梅克把一切都告诉我了。\n原来我们一直都看错了事情。

column5: At least, I know that I certainly was.\nI thought that my death in those tunnels would redeem me.\nBut now I know that my fate lies elsewhere — in Balteus.
column6: 至少，我知道我肯定错了。\n我以为在那些隧道里死去就能赎罪。\n但现在我知道，我的命运在别处——在巴尔泰乌斯。
