column5: Turning around to face the deck, I notice that Sovy is waving me over.{w}\nI walk toward him, wondering what it could be about. This seems important.{w}\nAs I make my way across the ship, I notice all my comrades scurrying about.
column6: 我转身面向甲板，注意到索维在朝我招手。{w}\n我朝他走去，想知道是为了什么。这事似乎很重要。{w}\n我穿过船只时，注意到我的同伴们都在匆匆忙忙地走动。

column5: I'm glad that they put us all on the same boat.\nI must say — I've gotten used to you and your friends.\nBeing placed anywhere else would be pretty uncomfortable.
column6: 我很高兴他们把我们安排在同一条船上。\n不得不说——我已经习惯了你和你的朋友们。\n被安排到别处会让我很不自在。

column5: I just wanted to tell you that I gave Damek some information.\nHe's forming a plan of attack as we speak, so it definitely helped.\nWhen it comes to Balteus and The Triumvirate, I know more than anybody.
column6: 我只是想告诉你，我给了达梅克一些情报。\n他此刻正在制定进攻计划，所以这肯定帮上了忙。\n说到巴尔泰乌斯和三人执政团，我比任何人都了解。

column5: I'm sorry for what we did to him during our attack, by the way.\nI ordered Shane to stab him, so it's technically my fault.\nHe seems fine though — so no hard feelings...?
column6: 顺便说，我为我们在袭击中对他做的事感到抱歉。\n是我下令让肖恩刺他的，所以严格来说是我的错。\n不过他看起来没事——那就别记恨我了……？

column5: I shrug, uncertain of how to respond.{w}\nIf it happened any differently, he'd be dead for sure.{w}\nIt feels a bit beyond coincidence, but I don't stop to question it.
column6: 我耸耸肩，不知道该如何回应。{w}\n要是稍有不同，他肯定就死了。{w}\n这感觉有点不像是巧合，但我没停下来深究。

column5: They might not tell your allies that I gave them this information, though.\nNot everybody trusts me, so it would probably just cause more harm than good.\nI'm not here to cause harm, so we all agreed it was best to \"omit\" a few facts.
column6: 不过，他们可能不会告诉你的盟友这情报是我给的。\n不是每个人都信任我，说了大概只会弊大于利。\n我不是来惹麻烦的，所以我们都同意，最好“省略”一些事实。

column5: It makes sense, so I understand where they're coming from.{w}\nFighting amongst ourselves is the last thing we need before the final battle.{w}\nIt was a time to stand strong, and united. A time to trust one another unconditionally.
column6: 这说得通，所以我理解他们的顾虑。{w}\n在最终决战之前，我们最不需要的就是内斗。{w}\n现在是坚强、团结的时候。是彼此无条件信任的时候。

column5: That's it, really. I just thought you deserved to know it came from me.\nI {i}did{/i} promise information that would help your final attack, after all.\nIf anything else comes to mind, I'll make sure to bring it to attention.
column6: 就这样，真的。我只是觉得你应该知道这情报是我提供的。\n毕竟我{i}确实{/i}承诺过会提供有助于你们最后进攻的情报。\n如果我还想到别的，一定会提出来。

column5: He's definitely going to great lengths to make himself seem genuine.{w}\nThat's good. There was a lot of doubt in the air surrounding this alliance.{w}\nThe people may not know he tipped us off, but they didn't really have to.
column6: 他确实费尽心思让自己显得诚恳。{w}\n这是好事。围绕这次结盟的疑虑一直很多。{w}\n人们也许不知道是他给我们通风报信，但他们其实也没必要知道。

column5: He turns away from me, and stares into the distance. I guess this talk is over.{w}\nI decide to make my way to Damek and Howl to see what information he gave them.{w}\nBut before I can get there, I'm interrupted by my comrades. They seem really excited.
column6: 他转身背对我，望向远方。看来这次谈话结束了。{w}\n我决定去找达梅克和豪尔，看看他给了他们什么情报。{w}\n但我还没走到，就被同伴们打断了。他们看起来非常兴奋。

column5: We exchange hugs and pleasantries for a few moments.{w}\nAre they really happy? Or are they just putting on an act?{w}\nIt's hard to tell — since this is the calm before the storm.
column6: 我们拥抱寒暄了一阵。{w}\n他们是真的开心吗？还是只是在演戏？{w}\n很难分辨——毕竟这是暴风雨前的平静。

column5: I just wanted to tell you that I gave Howl some information.\nHe's forming a plan of attack as we speak, so it definitely helped.\nWhen it comes to Balteus and The Triumvirate, I know more than anybody.
column6: 我只是想告诉你，我给了豪尔一些情报。\n他此刻正在制定进攻计划，所以这肯定帮上了忙。\n说到巴尔泰乌斯和三人执政团，我比任何人都了解。

column5: But I guess he knows a bit about Balteus as well.\nI find it hard to believe that there's a legion of spirits inside of him.\nCrazier things have happened, I guess. It's just — really interesting.
column6: 不过我猜他对巴尔泰乌斯也有些了解。\n我很难相信他体内寄居着一整支灵军团。\n更离奇的事也发生过，我想。只是——真的很有意思。

column5: If he survives the war, I'd love to learn more about The Monarchy.\nYou should study them as well — since you're next in line for the throne.\nIt might be helpful to know what legacy you're carrying on, right...?
column6: 如果他能活过这场战争，我很想多了解一些王室的事。\n你也该研究研究他们——毕竟你是王位的下一任继承人。\n知道自己在继承什么样的遗产，也许会有帮助，对吧……？

column5: That's true — but there would be a better time and place.{w}\nRight now my main focus was taking down The Triumvirate.{w}\nUntil the throne was mine, all of that should be off the table.
column6: 这话不假——但会有更好的时间和场合。{w}\n眼下我的主要目标是打倒三人执政团。{w}\n在王位归我之前，那些事都该先搁置。

column5: Sovy nods, and decides to change the subject.{w}\nIt's remarkable how easy it was to get along with him.{w}\nUntil just recently, he seemed like such a cold, heartless killer.
column6: 索维点点头，决定换个话题。{w}\n跟他相处竟然如此轻松，真令人意外。{w}\n直到不久之前，他还像个冷酷无情的杀手。

column5: They might not tell your allies that I gave them this information, though.\nNot everybody trusts me, so it would probably just cause more harm than good.\nI'm not here to cause harm, so we all agreed it was best to \"omit\" a few facts.
column6: 不过，他们可能不会告诉你的盟友这情报是我给的。\n不是每个人都信任我，说了大概只会弊大于利。\n我不是来惹麻烦的，所以我们都同意，最好“省略”一些事实。

column5: It makes sense, so I understand where they're coming from.{w}\nFighting amongst ourselves is the last thing we need before the final battle.{w}\nIt was a time to stand strong, and united. A time to trust one another unconditionally.
column6: 这说得通，所以我理解他们的顾虑。{w}\n在最终决战之前，我们最不需要的就是内斗。{w}\n现在是坚强、团结的时候。是彼此无条件信任的时候。

column5: That's it, really. I just thought you deserved to know it came from me.\nI {i}did{/i} promise information that would help your final attack, after all.\nIf anything else comes to mind, I'll make sure to bring it to attention.
column6: 就这样，真的。我只是觉得你应该知道这情报是我提供的。\n毕竟我{i}确实{/i}承诺过会提供有助于你们最后进攻的情报。\n如果我还想到别的，一定会提出来。

column5: He's definitely going to great lengths to make himself seem genuine.{w}\nThat's good. There was a lot of doubt in the air surrounding this alliance.{w}\nThe people may not know he tipped us off, but they didn't really have to.
column6: 他确实费尽心思让自己显得诚恳。{w}\n这是好事。围绕这次结盟的疑虑一直很多。{w}\n人们也许不知道是他给我们通风报信，但他们其实也没必要知道。

column5: He turns away from me, and stares into the distance. I guess this talk is over.{w}\nI decide to make my way to Damek and Howl to see what information he gave them.{w}\nBut before I can get there, I'm interrupted by my comrades. They seem really excited.
column6: 他转身背对我，望向远方。看来这次谈话结束了。{w}\n我决定去找达梅克和豪尔，看看他给了他们什么情报。{w}\n但我还没走到，就被同伴们打断了。他们看起来非常兴奋。

column5: We exchange hugs and pleasantries for a few moments.{w}\nAre they really happy? Or are they just putting on an act?{w}\nIt's hard to tell — since this is the calm before the storm.
column6: 我们拥抱寒暄了一阵。{w}\n他们是真的开心吗？还是只是在演戏？{w}\n很难分辨——毕竟这是暴风雨前的平静。

column5: I turn around to face the deck and crew. The atmosphere seems tense.{w}\nDamek and Howl almost immediately grouped together. They're inspecting parchments.{w}\nIt looks important, as they're locked in discussion. They don't seem to be arguing with one another.
column6: 我转身面向甲板和船员。气氛似乎很紧张。{w}\n达梅克和豪尔几乎立刻就凑到了一起。他们在查看羊皮纸。{w}\n那看起来很重要，他们正专注于讨论。他们似乎并没有在争吵。

column5: As I walk toward them to see what's happening, I'm immediately interrupted by my comrades.{w}\nHappy to see me aboard, there's a quick exchange of hugs and pleasantries. They seem excited.{w}\nPerhaps they really are. Or, perhaps, they're putting on an act to hide how frightened they are.
column6: 我朝他们走去，想看看发生了什么，却立刻被同伴们打断。{w}\n他们高兴看到我上了船，很快互相拥抱寒暄了一番。他们看起来很兴奋。{w}\n也许他们是真的兴奋。又或者，他们是在演戏，掩饰自己的恐惧。

column5: Either way, it's best to make the most of any happy moments.{w}\nThis was the calm before the storm. One final storm.
column6: 无论如何，都该尽情享受任何快乐的时刻。{w}\n这是暴风雨前的平静。最后一场暴风雨。

column5: Hey there, [firstname]!\nGlad to see you made it here.\nI'm happy we're all on the same boat.
column6: 你好啊，[firstname]！\n很高兴看到你也来了。\n我很开心我们都在同一条船上。

column5: Yeah, it makes me feel way better.\nIf I was stuck with other people, I'd be worried.\nBut in this situation, I'm not. I'm perfectly comfortable.
column6: 是啊，这让我安心多了。\n要是跟别人困在一起，我会担心。\n但眼下的情况，我一点也不担心。我完全自在。

column5: I'm just doing my best to hang in there...\nThis whole \"life at sea\" thing really isn't my style.\nI can't wait to get back and settle down for good.
column6: 我只是在尽力撑着……\n这种“海上生活”实在不合我的性子。\n我迫不及待想回去，彻底安顿下来。

column5: Knock on wood, Pro.\nDon't get arrogant before the final battle.\nThis is a huge gamble — you need to give it your all.
column6: 别把话说满，普洛。\n在最终决战前可别太自满。\n这是一场豪赌——你必须全力以赴。

column5: Me? Arrogant? Never.\nAnyway, I need to take my mind off of this water stuff.\nHow about we go sit in the crew quarters and play some cards?
column6: 我？自满？绝不会。\n总之，我得把心思从这水上移开。\n不如我们去船员舱坐着打几把牌？

column5: Sure. But I think Damek is about to make a speech.\nHe's been lost in conversation with Howl for a while now.\nI overheard them talking about our plan of attack in Balteus.
column6: 好啊。不过我想达梅克快要讲话了。\n他和豪尔聊了很久了。\n我无意中听到他们在谈我们在巴尔泰乌斯的进攻计划。

column5: Sure. But I think Howl is about to make a speech.\nHe's been lost in conversation with Damek for a while now.\nI think I heard them talking about our upcoming plan of attack.
column6: 好啊。不过我想豪尔快要讲话了。\n他和达梅克聊了很久了。\n我好像听到他们在谈我们接下来的进攻计划。

column5: Alright, alright — I can wait.\nMaybe you should get over there, [firstname].\nI'm pretty sure that's something you'll want to be a part of.
column6: 好吧，好吧——我可以等。\n也许你该过去那边，[firstname]。\n我很确定那是你会想参与的事。

column5: That's true, and I was making my way over there anyway.{w}\nUlric and Pro go about their business, but Valessa and Fortaime stay.
column6: 确实如此，我本来也正往那边去。{w}\n乌尔里克和普洛去忙自己的事了，但瓦莱莎和福泰姆留了下来。

column5: Good luck, [firstname].\nI hope we get to spend more time together, but I understand if we don't get to.\nThis is probably the most important moment of your life — so do whatever you need.
column6: 祝你好运，[firstname]。\n我希望我们能多相处一些时间，但要是没机会，我也理解。\n这大概是你一生中最重要的时刻——所以去做你需要做的事吧。

column5: Yeah — as much as we need you, I think the world needs you more.\nHopefully this isn't goodbye, but there's always the chance that it is.\nSince we're going to Balteus, we need to treat that as a real option.
column6: 是啊——尽管我们需要你，但我觉得这个世界更需要你。\n希望这不是告别，但总有可能就是。\n既然我们要去巴尔泰乌斯，就得把这种可能当真。

column5: It's true, as grim as it made the conversation feel.{w}\nBefore I can respond, they both step forward and hug me at the same time.{w}\nI let out a soft laugh, and wrap my arms around them. Together, we've all come so far.
column6: 确实如此，尽管这让谈话变得沉重。{w}\n我还没来得及回应，她们就一起上前抱住了我。{w}\n我轻声一笑，张开双臂回抱她们。我们一起走了这么远。

column5: Thanks for everything, [firstname].\nI think you have some planning to do, so I'll let you go.
column6: 谢谢你做的一切，[firstname]。\n我想你还有些计划要做，我就不留你了。

column5: Yeah. Just know that I'll {i}never{/i} forget our time together.\nIf we play our cards right, then we can have more of that after the war.\nI know things have been crazy, but with you two by my side, it's been easier.
column6: 是啊。只是你要知道，我{i}永远不会{/i}忘记我们共度的时光。\n如果我们走对了棋，战后还能有更多这样的日子。\n我知道这一路很疯狂，但有你们俩在我身边，一切都容易了些。

column5: With the hug broken, we nod at one another with big smiles.{w}\nI'm sure we'd see each other again, so I don't let it get me down.{w}\nThere was no way we'd get to the end of this without crossing paths again.
column6: 拥抱结束后，我们笑容满面地互相点头。{w}\n我相信我们还会再见的，所以没让自己消沉。{w}\n我们不可能走到最后都不再相遇。

column5: I make my way over to Damek and Howl, scanning my surroundings as I do.{w}\nOur Pirate allies run about the ship, making last minute preparations and adjustments.{w}\nIt's nice to know that we had their sailing expertise. So many important people were on board.
column6: 我朝达梅克和豪尔走去，一边走一边打量着四周。{w}\n我们的海盗盟友在船上四处奔忙，做着最后的准备和调整。{w}\n有他们的航海本领在，真让人安心。船上有这么多重要的人物。

column5: Because of that, something told me that our ship would be in the very front of the pack.{w}\nBut I wouldn't know for sure until I talked to Damek and Howl. They turn to face me.{w}\nI can tell that they're stressed out. It's apparent on their faces. I ask them what's up.
column6: 正因如此，我有种预感，我们的船会排在船队的最前面。{w}\n但在和达梅克、豪尔谈过之前，我还不能确定。他们转身面向我。{w}\n我看得出他们压力很大。这明明白白写在脸上。我问他们怎么了。

column5: Hey, [firstname]. We were just taking care of some planning.\nI think we have a pretty good idea of what we're going to do.\nNow that we've talked it out, I think our chances are great.
column6: 嘿，[firstname]。我们刚在处理一些计划。\n我想我们已经很清楚要做什么了。\n既然谈开了，我觉得我们胜算很大。

column5: Damek is correct. Our confidence has increased tenfold.\nThanks to some last minute information, we now have the edge.\nHopefully we can keep that when we put our plan into practice.
column6: 达梅克说得对。我们的信心增长了十倍。\n多亏了最后关头得到的情报，我们现在占了上风。\n希望把计划付诸实践时，我们还能保持这一点。

column5: They both glance over at Sovy. I know that he gave them the information.{w}\nI'm glad that they trusted him enough to base their plan around his intel.{w}\nBack when we left Alarinthia, our alliance and trust seemed so shaky.
column6: 他们俩都朝索维瞥了一眼。我知道那情报是他给的。{w}\n我很高兴他们信任他，甚至以他的情报为基础制定计划。{w}\n当初我们离开阿拉林西亚时，我们的结盟和信任还显得那么脆弱。

column5: They glance at the scrolls that they're holding.{w}\nI notice Gryz's signature on them, as well as a Mazean seal.{w}\nHe worked for The Triumvirate too, so I'm sure his intel would be valuable.
column6: 他们瞥了一眼手中握着的卷轴。{w}\n我注意到上面有格瑞兹的签名，还有一枚马泽奥的印章。{w}\n他也曾为三人执政团效力，所以我确信他的情报会很有价值。

column5: I guess I should tell everybody what we're planning, then.\nI'll go stand at the head of the ship — and give myself a platform.\nThey might want to hear from you too, [firstname]. So be ready.
column6: 那么，我想我该告诉大家我们的计划了。\n我会站到船头去——给自己搭个台子。\n他们可能也想听你说几句，[firstname]。所以做好准备。

column5: We would like to tell everybody what we're planning.\nIf we stand at the head of the ship, we'll have a better platform to speak.\nThey might want to hear from you too, [firstname]. So be prepared.
column6: 我们想告诉大家我们的计划。\n如果站在船头，我们会有个更好的讲话位置。\n他们可能也想听你说几句，[firstname]。所以做好准备。

column5: I stand back, and watch as he takes slow steps toward the head of the ship.{w}\nI didn't even know what they were planning — so I'd be learning at the same time.{w}\nHowever, due to the fact that they were working together, I knew we were in good hands.
column6: 我退到一旁，看着他一步步缓缓走向船头。{w}\n我甚至不知道他们的计划是什么——所以我会和大家同时得知。{w}\n不过，既然他们通力合作，我知道我们很稳妥。

column5: Alex watches him pass by, and I can tell that he's tired of waiting around.{w}\nIt wouldn't be much longer before we set sail, so I hope he can wait a bit longer.{w}\nOnce the pirates start preparing the ship to leave, their shouts would drown everything out.
column6: 亚历克斯看着他走过，我看得出他已经等得不耐烦了。{w}\n我们很快就要启航了，希望他能再等一会儿。{w}\n一旦海盗们开始为出发做准备，他们的喊声会盖过一切。

column5: Nada watches him pass by, and I can tell that she's tired of waiting around.{w}\nIt wouldn't be much longer before we set sail, so I hope she can wait a bit longer.{w}\nOnce the pirates start preparing the ship to leave, their shouts would drown everything out.
column6: 娜达看着他走过，我看得出她已经等得不耐烦了。{w}\n我们很快就要启航了，希望她能再等一会儿。{w}\n一旦海盗们开始为出发做准备，他们的喊声会盖过一切。

column5: After a few more moments, he reaches the head of the ship, and clears his throat.{w}\nGathering the attention of everybody nearby, he mounts a crate to get higher ground.{w}\nA silence overtakes the entire ship. But he has no problem rising to overcome it.
column6: 又过了片刻，他走到船头，清了清嗓子。{w}\n他吸引了附近所有人的注意，爬上一个木箱以站得更高。{w}\n整艘船陷入沉默。但他毫不费力地开口，压过了这份寂静。

column5: Well, I guess this is the eve of our final attack.\nI know many of you are wondering just what's going to happen.\nI'll explain more later — but right now, I can tell you a {i}bit{/i} of what we're planning.
column6: 那么，我想这就是我们最后进攻的前夜了。\n我知道你们很多人都想知道究竟会发生什么。\n我稍后会详细说明——但现在，我可以告诉你们我们计划的{i}一部分{/i}。

column5: We should arrive in Balteus just as the sun is rising.\nWhen we do — we'll all be meeting at a central location for one final meeting.\nIt's important that everybody is on the same page before we take any big steps.
column6: 我们大概会在太阳升起时抵达巴尔泰乌斯。\n到那时——我们会在一个中心地点集合，开最后一次会。\n在采取任何重大行动之前，所有人达成共识很重要。

column5: However, our first big step will be to secure The Grand Library.\nHolding the proprieter hostage, we'll station our army there as a pseudo-HQ.\nI bet you're wondering why we've chosen the library. Well, our reasoning is twofold.
column6: 不过，我们的第一个重大行动是拿下大图书馆。\n我们会扣押馆主作为人质，把军队驻扎在那里，当作临时总部。\n我打赌你们在想为什么选图书馆。我们的理由有两点。

column5: First of all — we've been told that The Honor Guard cannot set foot inside.\nThere's some sort of ward on the property. Presumably so the owner can be alone.\nWe're not sure why they prefer to work alone, but we know they're important to The Triumvirate.
column6: 首先——我们听说荣誉卫队不能踏进那里。\n那片产业上有某种结界。大概是为了让主人能独处。\n我们不确定他们为何偏好独自工作，但我们知道他们对三人执政团很重要。

column5: That is part of our second reason. Taking them hostage, we will extract information.\nWe need anything we can gather that will help us with our next step — the final attack.\nWhile information is extracted, we can use the safety of the library to rest and recuperate.
column6: 这也是我们第二个理由的一部分。抓住他们当人质，我们就能获取情报。\n我们需要尽可能搜集一切有助于下一步——最终进攻——的东西。\n在获取情报的同时，我们可以利用图书馆的安全来休整恢复。

column5: After that rest, we will gather one more time, and begin our final assault.\n[firstname] will lead a small team, and infiltrate the castle, attacking The Triumvirate directly.\nThe rest of us will lead The Honor Guard to the Town Square, and fight them there as a distraction.
column6: 休整之后，我们会再次集结，开始最后的进攻。\n[firstname] 会带领一支小队潜入城堡，直接攻击三人执政团。\n我们其余的人会把荣誉卫队引到城镇广场，在那里与他们交战，作为牵制。

column5: With a distraction as large as we're planning, [firstname] should be unimpeded.\nHe will kill The Triumvirate, and destroy the large idol at the back of their chambers.\nWe believe this idol to be of importance to them, so we must destroy it in order to win.
column6: 有了我们计划中如此大规模的牵制，[firstname] 应该不会受阻。\n他会杀掉三人执政团，并摧毁他们内殿后方的那座大灵像。\n我们相信这座灵像对他们很重要，所以必须摧毁它才能取胜。

column5: With the blade plunged into that idol — [firstname] will tap into its power.\nHe will use it to deactivate The Honor Guard, and the suits of armor will crumble.\nAt that point, victory is ours. We will gather in the castle atrium and count the survivors.
column6: 把剑刺入那座灵像——[firstname] 就能汲取它的力量。\n他会用它让荣誉卫队失效，那些铠甲也会随之崩解。\n到那时，胜利就是我们的了。我们会在城堡中庭集合，清点幸存者。

column5: With a distraction as large as we're planning, [firstname] should be unimpeted.\nShe will kill The Triumvirate, and destroy the large idol at the back of their chambers.\nWe believe this idol to be importance to them, so we must destroy it right away.
column6: 有了我们计划中如此大规模的牵制，[firstname] 应该不会受阻。\n她会杀掉三人执政团，并摧毁他们内殿后方的那座大灵像。\n我们相信这座灵像对他们很重要，所以必须立刻摧毁它。

column5: With the blade plunged into that idol — [firstname] will tap into its power.\nAs it fades away, she will use its energy to deactivate every member of The Honor Guard.\nAt that point, victory is ours. We will gather in the castle atrium and count the survivors.
column6: 把剑刺入那座灵像——[firstname] 就能汲取它的力量。\n随着它消散，她会用它的能量让荣誉卫队的每一名成员失效。\n到那时，胜利就是我们的了。我们会在城堡中庭集合，清点幸存者。

column5: Everybody looks at me as Damek explains this part of the plan.{w}\nIt's my first time hearing it, but all of it makes perfect sense. It's a good strategy.{w}\nWe don't know what the idol is, but I could definitely use its power, like I did in our HQ.
column6: 达梅克解释计划的这一部分时，所有人都看着我。{w}\n我也是第一次听说，但一切都非常合理。这是个好策略。{w}\n我们不知道那灵像是什么，但我肯定能利用它的力量，就像我在总部里那样。

column5: With The Triumvirate dead, and their Honor Guard dissolved, victory was ours.{w}\nWe'd still have to worry about Halin and Shane, but I'm sure they'd pop up somewhere.{w}\nI feel confident. Giving everybody a nod, they turn their attention back to Damek's platform.
column6: 三人执政团一死，他们的荣誉卫队一瓦解，胜利就是我们的了。{w}\n我们还得提防哈林和肖恩，但我确信他们会在某处冒出来。{w}\n我很有信心。我朝众人点点头，他们便把注意力转回了达梅克的台子上。

column5: As soon as we arrive, I'll share this plan with everybody else.\nSo, until then — I'd advise getting some rest. You're going to need it.\nThat is, unless there's anything you want to say to all of us, [firstname]?
column6: 我们一抵达，我就会把这个计划告诉其他人。\n所以在那之前——我建议你们去休息一下。你们会需要的。\n除非你有什么想对我们大家说的，[firstname]？

column5: Here we stand — on the eve of our final attack.\nWe know that many of you are wondering what is going to happen.\nWe can share a bit of information, but the rest must wait until later.
column6: 我们站在这里——在最后进攻的前夜。\n我们知道你们很多人都想知道会发生什么。\n我们可以分享一部分情报，但其余的必须等到之后。

column5: We should arrive in Balteus, just as the sun is rising.\nWhen we do, we'll meet in a central location for one final meeting.\nIt's important to get everybody up to speed before taking any big steps.
column6: 我们大概会在太阳升起时抵达巴尔泰乌斯。\n到那时，我们会在一个中心地点集合，开最后一次会。\n在采取任何重大行动之前，让所有人了解情况很重要。

column5: Our first big step, however — is to secure The Grand Library.\nHolding the owner hostage, we'll station ourselves there as a new HQ.\nIf you're wondering why we've chosen that location, our reasoning is twofold.
column6: 不过，我们的第一个重大行动是拿下大图书馆。\n我们会扣押馆主作为人质，把自己驻扎在那里，当作新总部。\n如果你在想我们为什么选那个地方，我们的理由有两点。

column5: We've learned that The Honor Guard cannot set foot inside the property.\nThere's some sort of ward in effect. Presumably so the owner can be alone.\nWe're not sure why they require this — but we know they're important to our enemy.
column6: 我们得知荣誉卫队不能踏进那片产业。\n那里有某种结界在起作用。大概是为了让主人能独处。\n我们不确定他们为何需要如此——但我们知道他们对敌人很重要。

column5: That is part of our second reason. With them as our hostage, we can extract information.\nWe need every bit of intel we can get — anything to help us in our next step — the final attack.\nWhile information is extracted, we can use the safety of the library to rest and recuperate.
column6: 这也是我们第二个理由的一部分。有他们作人质，我们就能获取情报。\n我们需要尽可能搜集每一点情报——一切有助于下一步——最终进攻——的东西。\n在获取情报的同时，我们可以利用图书馆的安全来休整恢复。

column5: After that rest, we will gather one more time, and begin our final assault. This will be the end.\n[firstname] will lead a small team, and infiltrate the castle, attacking The Triumvirate directly.\nThe rest of us will lure The Honor Guard to the Town Square, and fight them there as a distraction.
column6: 休整之后，我们会再次集结，开始最后的进攻。这将是一切的终结。\n[firstname] 会带领一支小队潜入城堡，直接攻击三人执政团。\n我们其余的人会把荣誉卫队引到城镇广场，在那里与他们交战，作为牵制。

column5: With a distraction as large as we're planning, [firstname] should be unimpeded.\nHe will kill The Triumvirate, and destroy the large idol at the back of their chambers.\nWe believe this idol to be of importance to them, so we must destroy it promptly.
column6: 有了我们计划中如此大规模的牵制，[firstname] 应该不会受阻。\n他会杀掉三人执政团，并摧毁他们内殿后方的那座大灵像。\n我们相信这座灵像对他们很重要，所以必须迅速摧毁它。

column5: With the blade plunged into that idol — [firstname] will tap into its power.\nHe will use it to deactivate The Honor Guard, and the suits of armor will crumble.\nAt that point, victory is ours. We will gather in the castle atrium and count the survivors.
column6: 把剑刺入那座灵像——[firstname] 就能汲取它的力量。\n他会用它让荣誉卫队失效，那些铠甲也会随之崩解。\n到那时，胜利就是我们的了。我们会在城堡中庭集合，清点幸存者。

column5: With a distraction as large as we're planning, [firstname] should be unimpeded.\nShe will kill The Triumvirate, and destroy the large idol at the back of their chambers.\nWe believe this idol to be of importance to them, so we must destroy it in order to win.
column6: 有了我们计划中如此大规模的牵制，[firstname] 应该不会受阻。\n她会杀掉三人执政团，并摧毁他们内殿后方的那座大灵像。\n我们相信这座灵像对他们很重要，所以必须摧毁它才能取胜。

column5: With the blade plunged into that idol — [firstname] will tap into its power.\nShe will use it to deactivate The Honor Guard, and the suits of armor will crumble.\nAt that point, victory is ours. We will gather in the castle atrium and count the survivors.
column6: 把剑刺入那座灵像——[firstname] 就能汲取它的力量。\n她会用它让荣誉卫队失效，那些铠甲也会随之崩解。\n到那时，胜利就是我们的了。我们会在城堡中庭集合，清点幸存者。

column5: Everybody looks at me as Howl explains this part of the plan.{w}\nIt's my first time hearing it, but all of it makes perfect sense. It's a good strategy.{w}\nWe don't know what the idol is, but I could definitely use its power, like I did in our HQ.
column6: 豪尔解释计划的这一部分时，所有人都看着我。{w}\n我也是第一次听说，但一切都非常合理。这是个好策略。{w}\n我们不知道那灵像是什么，但我肯定能利用它的力量，就像我在总部里那样。

column5: With The Triumvirate dead, and their Honor Guard dissolved, victory was ours.{w}\nWe'd still have to worry about Halin and Shane, but I'm sure they'd pop up somewhere.{w}\nI feel confident. Giving everybody a nod, they turn their attention back to Damek's platform.
column6: 三人执政团一死，他们的荣誉卫队一瓦解，胜利就是我们的了。{w}\n我们还得提防哈林和肖恩，但我确信他们会在某处冒出来。{w}\n我很有信心。我朝众人点点头，他们便把注意力转回了达梅克的台子上。

column5: As soon as we arrive, we will share this plan with everybody else.\nSo, until then — we'd advise getting some rest. You're going to need it.\nThat is, unless there's anything you'd like to say to us, [firstname]...?
column6: 我们一抵达，就会把这个计划告诉其他人。\n所以在那之前——我们建议你们去休息一下。你们会需要的。\n除非你有什么想对我们说的，[firstname]……？

column5: All eyes are on me once again, and I take a few steps forward.{w}\nDamek jumps off of the crate, leaving me a platform to stand on.{w}\nA speech...? I've never given one of those in my life. I don't know.
column6: 所有的目光又一次落在我身上，我向前走了几步。{w}\n达梅克跳下木箱，给我留下一个可以站上去的台子。{w}\n演讲……？我这辈子从没做过这种事。我不知道。

column5: All eyes are on me once again, and I take a few steps forward.{w}\nHowl jumps off of the crate, leaving me a platform to stand on.{w}\nA speech...? I've never given one of those in my life. I don't know.
column6: 所有的目光又一次落在我身上，我向前走了几步。{w}\n豪尔跳下木箱，给我留下一个可以站上去的台子。{w}\n演讲……？我这辈子从没做过这种事。我不知道。

column5: My uncertainty must come across in my demeanor, as they start urging me on.{w}\nThey even break away from each other, leaving a clear path for me to walk forward.{w}\nI {i}am{/i} technically their leader. It makes sense for me to talk. I'd have to get used to this.
column6: 我的迟疑一定从举止中流露了出来，因为他们开始催促我。{w}\n他们甚至彼此散开，为我让出一条前行的通道。{w}\n严格来说，我{i}确实{/i}是他们的领袖。由我来说话也合理。我得习惯这种事。

column5: I continue to walk forward, and notice smiles appear on their faces.{w}\nThe impact that my actions and attitude have on everybody here is very clear.{w}\nIt's a good thing that this level of responsibility was given to someone who can handle it.
column6: 我继续向前走，注意到他们脸上露出了笑容。{w}\n我的一举一动、一言一行对这里所有人的影响都很明显。{w}\n还好，这份重担交给了能担得起的人。

column5: A few moments later, I'm on top of the crate, matching the deep gaze of all my subjects.{w}\nSilence overtakes everything. I can hear the calm of the water against the docks of Mazeo.{w}\nIt was clear that I'd have to break this silence. I clear my throat, and think of what I should say.
column6: 片刻之后，我站上木箱，与所有臣民深沉的目光相接。{w}\n寂静笼罩了一切。我能听到海水轻拍马泽奥码头的平静声响。{w}\n显然，我必须打破这份沉默。我清了清嗓子，思考该说什么。

column5: They start to mutter amongst themselves, nodding in agreement with everything I say.
column6: 他们开始在下面低声议论，对我说的每句话都点头赞同。

column5: A bunch of them start cheering, with wide grins on their faces.{w}\nI'm speaking from the heart — speaking from instinct — and it's working.{w}\nI smile now too, and my words from this moment on are filled with confidence.
column6: 他们中有一群人开始欢呼，咧开嘴笑得灿烂。{w}\n我在凭心声说话——凭本能说话——而且奏效了。{w}\n现在我也笑了，从这一刻起，我的话语充满了自信。

column5: The crowd is roaring with applause, cheering on my every word.{w}\nI know they want more, so I try and think of what I should say next.
column6: 人群爆发出掌声，为我说的每一句话喝彩。{w}\n我知道他们想要更多，于是我努力想接下来该说什么。

column5: I grab the blade from my back, and slowly unsheathe it.
column6: 我从背后抽出那把剑，缓缓拔剑出鞘。

column5: Holding the blade out, they explode with even more applause.{w}\nI held a symbol that almost guaranteed our victory — and our freedom.{w}\nNobody has ever had, or ever will, have a better chance of taking them down.
column6: 我举起剑，他们的掌声更加爆发。{w}\n我握着的，是一个几乎能确保我们胜利——以及我们的自由——的象征。{w}\n从来没有人——也永远不会有人——有比这更好的机会将他们扳倒。

column5: I put the blade back in its scabbard, signalling that I'm almost done speaking.{w}\nRaising my fist in the air, I give out one last shout. One last call to unify our cause.
column6: 我把剑收回剑鞘，示意我快说完了。{w}\n我举起拳头，发出最后一声呐喊。最后一次召唤，让我们的事业团结一心。

column5: With a wide smile, and met with a large round of applause, I jump off the crate.{w}\nTaking it as a sign that we're ready to depart, the pirates start preparing to set sail.{w}\nI should probably meet with Damek and Howl one last time before deciding what to do.
column6: 我咧嘴一笑，在一大阵掌声中跳下木箱。{w}\n海盗们把这当作我们准备出发的信号，开始为启航做准备。{w}\n在决定下一步该做什么之前，我也许该最后再和达梅克、豪尔见一面。

column5: As I approach them, I notice they look happier than I've ever seen.{w}\nI never saw myself as a public speaker, so I'm quite surprised at what happened.{w}\nDoubts of my efficacy were still there, but seeing my comrades smile helped that worry dissipate.
column6: 我走近他们，注意到他们看起来比以往任何时候都开心。{w}\n我从不觉得自己擅长公开讲话，所以刚才发生的事让我相当意外。{w}\n对自身能力的怀疑仍在，但看到同伴们的笑容，那份担忧也随之消散。

column5: Eloquently put, [firstname].\nBetter than my own speeches, I have to admit.\nI could see just how much everybody looks up to you.
column6: 说得很有感染力，[firstname]。\n我得承认，比我自己的演讲还好。\n我能看出大家有多仰慕你。

column5: It was quite impressive, we must say.\nYou're going to make a fine leader — we're sure of it.\nThe greatest asset of any ruler is the ability to inspire hope.
column6: 不得不说，相当令人印象深刻。\n你会成为一个出色的领袖——我们很确定。\n任何统治者最大的资本，就是激励希望的能力。

column5: And I'd say we have that in droves, now.\nI trust that you're okay with our plan, [firstname]...?\nSorry that we didn't have time to pass it by you first.
column6: 而我觉得我们现在最不缺的就是这个。\n我相信你对我们的计划没有异议，[firstname]……？\n抱歉我们没时间先跟你商量。

column5: I nod. It all seems good.
column6: 我点点头。看起来一切都没问题。

column5: Good. It seems that everything is now in order.\nPerhaps you should go and get some rest, [firstname].\nWe will wake you if there are any matters of importance.
column6: 很好。看来现在一切都安排妥当了。\n也许你该去休息一下，[firstname]。\n如果有任何重要的事，我们会叫醒你。

column5: Yeah, we need you rested when we reach Balteus.\nYou know our plan, and the pirates are about to set sail.\nThere's nothing left for you to do. At least, for now.
column6: 是啊，抵达巴尔泰乌斯时我们需要你精力充沛。\n你已经知道我们的计划，海盗们也快启航了。\n没有你还要做的事了。至少，眼下没有。

column5: I guess he was right. Until we arrived, things were out of my hands.{w}\nAfter thanking them for the opportunity, I make my way to the crew quarters.{w}\nI value the opportunity to rest — but given the circumstances — that rest won't come easy.
column6: 我想他说得对。在抵达之前，事情都不由我掌控。{w}\n谢过他们给我这个机会，我朝船员舱走去。{w}\n我珍惜这个休息的机会——但考虑到眼下的处境——这觉可不好睡。

column5: Halin and Shane gather at the docks of Balteus.{w}\nSurrounded by Honor Guard, they order them to prepare a small fleet.{w}\nThey knew the end was coming, and they had to meet it head on.
column6: 哈林和肖恩在巴尔泰乌斯的码头集结。{w}\n在荣誉卫队的簇拥下，他们下令准备一支小型船队。{w}\n他们知道终局将至，必须正面迎上。

column5: What was your reasoning behind this again...?\nI'm surprised The Triumvirate decided to play along with your plan.
column6: 再说一遍，你这么做的理由是什么……？\n我很意外三人执政团居然同意配合你的计划。

column5: They have to come by sea, and this is the main point of entry.\nIf we leave from here, we can intercept them before they arrive.\nThe plan is to thin out their numbers as early as possible.
column6: 他们只能走海路来，而这里是主要的入口。\n如果我们从这里出发，就能在他们抵达前拦截。\n计划就是尽早削减他们的兵力。

column5: What if this fails — and they sink our fleet?
column6: 要是失败了——他们击沉了我们的船队怎么办？

column5: Scared of dying, are you...?
column6: 你是怕死了吧……？

column5: No, that's not what I meant.\nIt's a valid concern, Shane.
column6: 不，我不是那个意思。\n这是个合理的担忧，肖恩。

column5: Well, in my case — I don't really have anything left to lose.\nLet me lead this charge myself, Halin. You can go back to the castle.\nYou'll be needed there for a second line of defense, if they make it that far.
column6: 嗯，就我而言——我已经没什么可失去的了。\n让我自己来带这次冲锋吧，哈林。你可以回城堡去。\n如果他们真能打到那里，需要你在那儿布置第二道防线。

column5: I trust that they won't...?
column6: 我相信他们打不到吧……？

column5: Me too. Just tell The Triumvirate I'll be there soon.\nI have no intention of dying. Not to any of those weaklings.
column6: 我也这么希望。告诉三人执政团我很快就到。\n我可不打算死。更不会死在那些废物手里。

column5: Shane instructs the Honor Guard to get on board the ships.{w}\nIt's a small fleet, of only a few ships. Halin watches, and scoffs.
column6: 肖恩吩咐荣誉卫队登船。{w}\n那是一支小型船队，只有寥寥几艘船。哈林在一旁看着，嗤笑一声。

column5: You have a death wish, you know that?\nI get that you hate them, but don't throw your life away.\nThe Triumvirate rewards service. Keep that in mind, alright?
column6: 你这是自寻死路，你知道吗？\n我明白你恨他们，但别把命丢了。\n三人执政团会奖赏有功之人。记住这一点，好吗？

column5: Don't worry. I know what I'm doing.\nI'll be back before you know it — so go and have a rest.\nJust wait, Halin. If they even arrive, you'll find that their hope is lost.
column6: 别担心。我知道自己在做什么。\n你一转眼我就回来了——所以去歇着吧。\n等着瞧吧，哈林。就算他们真来了，你会发现他们的希望早已破灭。

column5: Halin smiles. A sinister smirk.{w}\nHe knows exactly what Shane is implying.
column6: 哈林笑了。一个阴险的冷笑。{w}\n他完全明白肖恩在暗示什么。

column5: Very well — I can get behind that thought.\nBe careful, though. You're a good Apprentice, Shane.\nI trust that you and the Honor Guard will do some real damage.
column6: 很好——这个想法我支持。\n不过小心点。你是个好学徒，肖恩。\n我相信你和荣誉卫队能造成真正的打击。

column5: Yeah, that's the idea.\nI'll see you back at the castle?
column6: 对，正是这个打算。\n我们城堡见？

column5: Sure.
column6: 好。

column5: Halin starts to walk away, but quickly turns around.
column6: 哈林转身要走，却又很快回过头来。

column5: You know — Sovy never let me do stuff like this.\nAs his Apprentice, he shut down almost every plan I ever had.\nI have to be better than him, though. I'm trusting you with a lot here.
column6: 你知道吗——索维从不让我做这种事。\n作为他的学徒，我几乎所有计划都被他否掉了。\n不过我必须比他强。我在这里可是把很多事都托付给了你。

column5: Don't worry — I promise not to let you down.\nThe Rebellion ends today. You have my word, Master.
column6: 别担心——我保证不会让你失望。\n反抗军今天就会终结。我向你保证，师父。

column5: Halin nods, and starts making his way back to the castle.{w}\nShane remains, muttering to himself with trembling fists.
column6: 哈林点点头，动身返回城堡。{w}\n肖恩留在原地，双拳颤抖，低声自语。

column5: And it all starts with that little figurehead of theirs.\nIt's almost time, Seer. You'll be joining Damek soon enough.
column6: 一切都从他们那个小傀儡领袖开始。\n时间快到了，先知。你很快就会去陪达梅克了。

column5: And it all starts with that little figurehead of theirs.\nIt's almost time, Seeress. You'll be joining Damek soon enough.
column6: 一切都从他们那个小傀儡领袖开始。\n时间快到了，先知。你很快就会去陪达梅克了。

column5: I toss and turn, getting minimal amounts of sleep.{w}\nThe blade rests against my bed, ready to grab at a moment's notice.{w}\nI fade in and out of sleep — fighting a mixture of both anxiety and tranquility.
column6: 我翻来覆去，只睡了很少一会儿。{w}\n那把剑就靠在我床边，随时可以一把抓起。{w}\n我在睡与醒之间浮沉——与交织在一起的焦虑和安宁相抗争。

column5: Just when I'm about to fall asleep, a negative thought jolts me back awake.{w}\nWe had no idea what would happen when we arrived in Balteus. It was terrifying.{w}\nI realize that sleeping probably isn't going to happen right now, so I get out of the hard bed.
column6: 就在我快要睡着时，一个消极的念头又把我惊醒。{w}\n我们完全不知道抵达巴尔泰乌斯后会发生什么。这令人恐惧。{w}\n我意识到这会儿大概睡不着了，于是从硬邦邦的床上起身。

column5: Just as I do, I notice somebody approaching out of the corner of my eye.{w}\nGrabbing the blade, I prepare myself for anything out of a twisted paranoia.
column6: 就在我起身时，我眼角余光注意到有人正走近。{w}\n我抓起那把剑，出于一种扭曲的偏执，做好了应对任何情况的准备。

column5: Put that thing down, [firstname].\nIt's not the answer to all of your problems.
column6: 把那东西放下，[firstname]。\n它不是你所有问题的答案。

column5: It's just Draycu. That's a relief.
column6: 只是德雷库。真是松了口气。

column5: It appears that there's been some... complications.\nDamek wanted me to tell you that you're needed on deck.\nYou'll see what I mean when you get up there, alright?
column6: 看来出了一些……麻烦。\n达梅克让我转告你，甲板上需要你。\n你上去之后就明白我的意思了，好吗？

column5: I nod. It must be important if he's interrupting my rest.{w}\nAs I start to walk away, Draycu puts a hand on my shoulder.
column6: 我点点头。既然他会来打断我休息，那一定很重要。{w}\n我正要走开，德雷库却把手搭在了我肩上。

column5: And I just wanted to tell you that I know what happened in Alarinthia.\nI know that Pro and Ulric teamed up in order to throw our fight.
column6: 我还想告诉你，我知道在阿拉林西亚发生了什么。\n我知道普洛和乌尔里克联手，故意输掉了我们的那场比试。

column5: I gulp, unsure of how Draycu would react to such news.{w}\nBut much to my surprise, he lets out a hearty laugh.
column6: 我咽了口唾沫，不确定德雷库会如何回应这个消息。{w}\n但让我大为意外的是，他开怀大笑起来。

column5: I haven't been that amused in ages, to be honest. It was wonderful.\nVivien was obsessed with intelligence. Brains over brawn — that sort of thing.\nThere's a beautiful irony in outsmarting a man who prides himself on his intellect.
column6: 说实话，我已经很久没有这么觉得好笑了。真是精彩。\n薇薇安痴迷于智谋。崇尚智取而非蛮力——就是那种理念。\n智胜一个以才智自傲的人，这其中有种绝妙的讽刺。

column5: In addition to that, we sent a message to every Alarinthian.\nThose who wish to change our ways are doomed to failure.\nOthers may rise up, in time — but for now, my reign is safe.
column6: 除此之外，我们还向每一个阿拉林西亚人传递了一个讯息。\n那些企图改变我们规矩的人，注定失败。\n将来或许还会有别人崛起——但眼下，我的统治稳如磐石。

column5: And for that, I commend you.\nGood luck on deck. I think you'll need it.
column6: 为此，我赞许你。\n甲板上好运。我想你会需要的。
